# About this report

This report recomputes the numbers that Sections 2 to 5 and Appendices A, B and C of *Separate
Ways and the Upside Down* print, in R and without running the author's Python. The Python scripts were
read only for the method and the inputs. Each number the paper prints stands beside the value
computed here, with a tolerance, and is marked PASS or FAIL; the words of the paper that carry the
number are quoted beside it. A section of planted errors then shows that each check can fail.

To run it, from the directory that holds this file:

```
Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("VERIFY_v6.Rmd")'
```

It needs R with rmarkdown, knitr and cubature, and the three helper files `verify_v6_core.R`,
`verify_v6_amplitudes.R` and `verify_v6_modes.R` beside it. The R code takes about 10 s of
processor time on one core, and the author's checker in the last section a few seconds more. The
parameter `full_modes`, off by default, repeats the mode integration with twice the nodes, a later
end time and half the step, and doubles the R time:

```
Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("VERIFY_v6.Rmd", params = list(full_modes = TRUE))'
```

Numbers from Section 6 of the paper (observations) are left out, except the neutrino line at half
the ceiling mass, which follows from the ceiling. Literature values that the paper compares with
(Clery et al., Bernal et al., Garny et al., Tang and Wu, Boyle, Turok and Vaibhav, Han, Lykken and
Zhang, Shaposhnikov et al.) are read from those papers and marked as quoted.

# Comparison rule

Every comparison goes through one function, `judge()`. A check passes when the computed value lies
within the tolerance of the paper's value, and fails otherwise, including when the computed value
is missing or infinite. For a number the paper prints, the tolerance is half a unit in its last
printed digit, so `1.20e-2` admits 1.195e-2 to 1.205e-2. Exact forms such as π/15 are compared at a
relative tolerance of 1e-10 or as stated, and identities that should vanish at an absolute
tolerance. The column *In text* says whether the quoted words occur, verbatim up to white space, in
the paper source found beside this file: **`r if (is.na(PAPER_FILE)) "none found" else PAPER_FILE`**.

The helper files hold the comparison rule, the inputs, the Dirac algebra and stress tensors, and

# Inputs

Physical constants, as the author's scripts and the paper state them. Only these enter below.

```{r inputs-derived}
s0_GeV3 <- K("s0_cm3") * K("hbarc")^3
kT0 <- K("kB") * K("T0_K") * 1e-9                                  # GeV
s0_from_T0 <- (2 * pi^2 / 45) * (43 / 11) * (kT0 / K("hbarc"))^3    # cm^-3, g*s = 43/11
rho_s <- K("rho_DM") / s0_GeV3                                     # rho_DM,0 / s0 in GeV

chk("inp-1", "inp", "mu = (4 pi G/3)^(-1/2) = sqrt(3/4 pi) M_Pl, GeV", MU, "5.965e18",
    quote = r"($\mu=(4\pi G/3)^{-1/2}=\sqrt6\,M_P=5.965\times10^{18}$ GeV)", where = "Section 4.2")
chk("inp-2", "inp", "sqrt(6) M_P with M_P = 2.435e18 GeV", sqrt(6) * K("M_P"), "5.965e18",
    quote = r"($\mu=(4\pi G/3)^{-1/2}=\sqrt6\,M_P=5.965\times10^{18}$ GeV)", where = "Section 4.2")
chk("inp-3", "inp", "s0 = 2891.2 cm^-3 in GeV^3", s0_GeV3, "2.2215e-38",
    quote = r"($s_0=2891.2$ cm$^{-3}=2.2215\times10^{-38}$ GeV$^3$)", where = "Section 4.2")
chk("inp-4", "inp", "s0 rebuilt from T0 = 2.7255 K, (2 pi^2/45)(43/11) T0^3, cm^-3, against the standard 2891.2", s0_from_T0, 2891.2,
    rel = 1e-4, label = "2891.2 to 1e-4", quote = r"($s_0=2891.2$ cm$^{-3}=2.2215\times10^{-38}$ GeV$^3$ for $T_0=2.7255$ K)", where = "Section 4.2")
show_checks("inp")
```

With $g_{*s}=43/11$ the stated $T_0=2.7255$ K gives `r sprintf("%.2f", s0_from_T0)` cm$^{-3}$, and
with $g_{*s}$ rounded to 3.909 it gives `r sprintf("%.2f", s0_from_T0 * 3.909 / (43 / 11))` cm$^{-3}$.
The standard value, 2891.2 cm$^{-3}$, uses $g_{*s}=3.909$. Everything below uses it; the larger value would lower the mass ceiling by
`r sprintf("%.4f", 100 * (1 - (K("s0_cm3") / s0_from_T0)^0.4))` per cent.

# Mode equation near the bang

Section 3 writes each helicity component of a mode as
$i\,\partial_t\psi=(t\,\sigma_z+x\,\sigma_x)\psi$ with $t=\sqrt{Ma_1}\,\eta$ and
$x=p/\sqrt{Ma_1}$. The solver here is a fourth-order Runge-Kutta integration written in R
(`rk4_modes`), with each end point corrected to first order in the adiabatic expansion. Three
states are followed:

* the in-vacuum: a full sweep from $t=-T$ to $+T$, started in the ground level;
* the family $\psi(0)\propto(1,e^{i\varphi})$: the two basis states are evolved from $t=0$, and the
  late occupation $n(\varphi)$ is minimised and maximised over $\varphi$ in closed form;
* the massless vacuum at the bang, $\varphi=\pi$, the ground state of $x\sigma_x$.

```{r modes-run}
t_modes <- Sys.time()
fm <- isTRUE(params$full_modes)
## Gauss-Legendre nodes: two panels of 24 on [0, 4], 24 on [4, 10], 24 on [0, 3] (twice as many with full_modes)
nq <- if (fm) 48 else 24
q_main <- gl_nodes(0, 4, nq, 2); q_tail <- gl_nodes(4, 10, nq); q_sweep <- gl_nodes(0, 3, nq)
x_main <- q_main$x; x_tail <- q_tail$x
T_main <- if (fm) 40 else 30
step_c <- if (fm) 0.01 else 0.02
sweep <- full_sweep(q_sweep$x, T = 20, c = 1.5 * step_c)
hc <- half_crossing(x_main, T = T_main, c = step_c)
hc_tail <- half_crossing(x_tail, T = 40, c = 1.5 * step_c)
glq <- function(q, y) sum(q$w * y)

## full sweep: excitation probability against Landau-Zener
dev_P <- max(abs(sweep$P - exp(-pi * sweep$x^2)))
I_in_rk <- glq(q_sweep, sweep$x^2 * sweep$P) / sqrt(pi)            # tail beyond x = 3 is below 1e-12
I_in_cf <- 1 / (4 * pi^1.5)

## the family: least occupation over the phase, against the half-angle formula
dev_nstar <- max(abs(hc$nmin - n_star(x_main)))
dev_edge <- max(abs(hc$nmin + hc$nmax - 1))
I_star_cf <- integrate(function(x) x^2 * n_star(x), 0, Inf, rel.tol = 1e-13)$value / sqrt(pi)
I_star_rk <- glq(q_main, x_main^2 * hc$nmin) / sqrt(pi)            # tail beyond x = 4 is below 1e-20

## massless vacuum: mode integration against the Gamma-function form, the 1/(16 x^4) tail, and I
hc10 <- half_crossing(10, T = 40, c = 1.5 * step_c)
dev_nvac <- max(abs(c(hc$nvac - n_vac_cf(x_main), hc_tail$nvac - n_vac_cf(x_tail), hc10$nvac - n_vac_cf(10))))
tail16 <- 16 * 10^4 * hc10$nvac
I_vac_rk <- (glq(q_main, x_main^2 * hc$nvac) + glq(q_tail, x_tail^2 * hc_tail$nvac) +
             1 / (16 * 10)) / sqrt(pi)                              # beyond x = 10: Int x^2/(16 x^4)
I_vac_cf <- (integrate(function(x) x^2 * n_vac_cf(x), 0, 40, rel.tol = 1e-11, subdivisions = 500)$value +
             1 / (16 * 40)) / sqrt(pi)
t_modes <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t_modes, units = "secs"))

chk("mode-1", "mode", "full sweep: largest |P - exp(-pi x^2)| at the nodes", dev_P, 0, tol = 1e-6, label = "0",
    quote = r"(ends in the excited state with probability $P=e^{-\pi x^2}$)", where = "Section 3.1")
chk("mode-2", "mode", "I_in from the mode integration", I_in_rk, "0.04490",
    quote = r"($I_{\rm in}=1/(4\pi^{3/2})=0.04490$)", where = "Section 3.2")
chk("mode-3", "mode", "I_in = 1/(4 pi^(3/2))", I_in_cf, "0.04490",
    quote = r"($I_{\rm in}=1/(4\pi^{3/2})=0.04490$)", where = "Section 3.2")
chk("mode-4", "mode", "least occupation over the family: largest |n_min - n_*| at the nodes", dev_nstar, 0,
    tol = 1e-6, label = "0", quote = r"(n_*(x)=\tfrac12\Bigl(1-\sqrt{1-e^{-\pi x^2}}\Bigr))", where = "Section 3.2")
chk("mode-5", "mode", "upper edge of the family: largest |n_min + n_max - 1|", dev_edge, 0, tol = 1e-6, label = "0",
    quote = r"(the late occupation of a mode runs between $n_*$ and $1-n_*$)", where = "Appendix A")
chk("mode-6", "mode", "I_* from the closed form", I_star_cf, "0.0127597",
    quote = r"(which for this state is $I_*=0.0127597$)", where = "Section 3.2")
chk("mode-7", "mode", "I_* from the mode integration", I_star_rk, "0.0127597",
    quote = r"(which for this state is $I_*=0.0127597$)", where = "Section 3.2")
chk("mode-8", "mode", "massless vacuum: largest |n_vac(RK) - Gamma-function form|, x from 0 to 10", dev_nvac, 0,
    tol = 1e-6, label = "0", where = "cross-check")
chk("mode-9", "mode", "massless vacuum: 16 x^4 n_vac at x = 10", tail16, 1, rel = 1e-3, label = "1",
    quote = r"(its occupation falls only as $1/(16x^4)$)", where = "Section 3.2")
chk("mode-10", "mode", "massless vacuum: I from the mode integration plus the 1/(16 x^4) tail", I_vac_rk, "0.0642",
    quote = r"(its occupation falls only as $1/(16x^4)$, and $I=0.0642$)", where = "Section 3.2")
chk("mode-11", "mode", "massless vacuum: I from the Gamma-function form", I_vac_cf, "0.0642",
    quote = r"(its occupation falls only as $1/(16x^4)$, and $I=0.0642$)", where = "Section 3.2")
show_checks("mode")
```

The half crossing took `r hc$nstep` Runge-Kutta steps to the end time $T=`r T_main`$ for
`r length(x_main)` momenta at once, and the whole section `r sprintf("%.1f", t_modes)` s. The
integrals over $x$ use Gauss-Legendre nodes, at which the solver is evaluated directly. The Gamma-function form of the
massless-vacuum occupation,
$n=\tfrac12[1-\sqrt{1-e^{-\pi x^2}}\cos\vartheta]$ with
$\vartheta=\tfrac\pi4+\arg\Gamma(\tfrac12+\tfrac{ix^2}4)-\arg\Gamma(1+\tfrac{ix^2}4)$, is evaluated
with a complex log-gamma written here; the mode integration does not use it, and the two agree to
`r tex_sci(dev_nvac, 2)`.

# Mass ceiling

Section 4.2 turns the production integral into a mass,
$M^{5/2}=(\rho_{\rm DM,0}/s_0)(2\pi^2/45)\,g_*^{1/4}\,15^{3/4}\mu^{3/2}/I$. The formula is first
rebuilt from its parts: the comoving number $na^3=(Ma_1/\pi)^{3/2}I$, the radiation-era slope
$a_1=(aT)^2\pi\sqrt{g_*/15}/\mu$ and the entropy $sa^3=(2\pi^2/45)g_*(aT)^3$, solved for $M$ at two
values of $aT$ to show that $aT$ drops out.

```{r mass}
mass_by_parts <- function(I, aT) {
  a1 <- function(M) aT^2 * pi * sqrt(K("gstar") / 15) / MU
  f <- function(lM) { M <- exp(lM); M * (M * a1(M) / pi)^1.5 * I / ((2 * pi^2 / 45) * K("gstar") * aT^3) - rho_s }
  exp(uniroot(f, c(log(1e3), log(1e12)), tol = 1e-14)$root)
}
M_star <- mass_from_I(I_star_cf)
M_star_rk <- mass_from_I(I_star_rk)
M_parts <- c(mass_by_parts(I_star_cf, 1), mass_by_parts(I_star_cf, 7.3))
Omega_from_rho <- K("rho_DM") / (K("rho_crit") * K("hbarc")^3)
M_planck <- M_star * (K("Omega_c") / Omega_from_rho)^0.4
dM_planck <- 0.4 * K("Omega_err") / K("Omega_c") * M_planck
M_bft_s0 <- mass_from_I(I_star_cf, s0 = K("s0_BFT"))
M_F2 <- M_star * 2^0.4
dM_g <- mass_from_I(I_star_cf, g = 110.25) - M_star

chk("mass-1", "mass", "M from the formula against M from its parts, aT = 1 and 7.3 (largest relative gap)",
    max(abs(M_parts / M_star - 1)), 0, tol = 1e-9, label = "0",
    quote = r"(Since the factors of $aT$ cancel)", where = "Section 4.2")
chk("mass-2", "mass", "M_* from I_* (closed form), PeV", M_star / 1e6, "491.6",
    quote = r"(M_*=491.6\ {\rm PeV})", where = "Section 4.2")
chk("mass-3", "mass", "M_* from I_* (mode integration), PeV", M_star_rk / 1e6, "491.6",
    quote = r"(M_*=491.6\ {\rm PeV})", where = "Section 4.2")
chk("mass-4", "mass", "Omega_c h^2 of rho_DM,0 = 9.7e-48 GeV^4", Omega_from_rho, "0.1198",
    quote = r"(Boyle, Finn and Turok's $\rho_{\rm DM,0}$ corresponds to $\Omega_ch^2=0.1198$)", where = "Section 4.2")
chk("mass-5", "mass", "M at Planck's Omega_c h^2 = 0.1200, PeV", M_planck / 1e6, "491.9",
    quote = r"(gives $491.9\pm2.0$ PeV)", where = "Section 4.2")
chk("mass-6", "mass", "its error from 0.0012, PeV", dM_planck / 1e6, "2.0",
    quote = r"(gives $491.9\pm2.0$ PeV)", where = "Section 4.2")
chk("mass-7", "mass", "every mass at Planck's value over the same at the paper's: 491.9 over 491.6", M_planck / M_star,
    491.9 / 491.6, rel = 2e-4, label = "491.9/491.6", quote = r"(would rise in the same proportion)", where = "Section 4.2")
chk("mass-8", "mass", "M with s0 = 2.3e-38 GeV^3, PeV", M_bft_s0 / 1e6, "484.8",
    quote = r"(which on its own gives 484.8 PeV)", where = "Section 4.2")
chk("mass-9", "mass", "the same, GeV, against Boyle, Finn and Turok's figure", M_bft_s0, "4.8e8",
    quote = r"(Their own $4.8\times10^8$ GeV)", where = "Section 4.2")
chk("mass-10", "mass", "entropy release F = 2: M_* 2^(2/5), PeV", M_F2 / 1e6, "648.7",
    quote = r"($F=2$ gives 648.7 PeV)", where = "Section 4.2")
chk("mass-11", "mass", "g* = 110.25: rise of the ceiling, PeV", dM_g / 1e6, "1.6",
    quote = r"($g_*=110.25$ and the ceiling rises by 1.6 PeV)", where = "Section 4.2")
chk("mass-12", "mass", "neutrino line at M_*/2, PeV", M_star / 2e6, "245.8",
    quote = r"(its neutrino line lies at or below 245.8 PeV)", where = "Abstract")
show_checks("mass")
```

With $\mu$ from Newton's constant, $M_*=`r sprintf("%.3f", M_star/1e6)`$ PeV. With
$\mu=\sqrt6\times2.435\times10^{18}$ GeV instead it is
`r sprintf("%.3f", mass_from_I(I_star_cf, mu = sqrt(6) * K("M_P"))/1e6)` PeV, the same to the
printed digit.

# Operator inequality

Section 4.1 and Appendix A: the Fock space of one pair is built by a Jordan-Wigner construction,
the before-region operators $a_-=c\,a_++s\,b_+^\dagger$ and $b_-=c\,b_+-s\,a_+^\dagger$ are formed
with $c^2+s^2=1$ and $s^2=P$, and the statements of the lemma are checked for
$P=0.05,0.2,0.5,0.8,0.95$. Each entry below is the worst case over these values of $P$.

```{r lemma}
sm <- matrix(c(0, 0, 1, 0), 2)           # lowering operator on one mode, basis (|0>, |1>)
Zp <- diag(c(1, -1)); Id2 <- diag(2)
jw <- function(k, n) Reduce(kronecker, c(rep(list(Zp), k), list(sm), rep(list(Id2), n - k - 1)))
dag <- function(A) t(Conj(A))
acomm <- function(A, B) A %*% B + B %*% A
set.seed(7)
worst <- c(car = 0, formula = 0, eig = 0, block = 0, saturate = 0, below = 0, qblock = 0)
vac_below <- TRUE
for (P in c(0.05, 0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 0.95)) {
  cc <- sqrt(1 - P); ss <- sqrt(P); ns <- (1 - sqrt(1 - P)) / 2
  a <- jw(0, 2); b <- jw(1, 2)
  am <- cc * a + ss * dag(b); bm <- cc * b - ss * dag(a)
  car <- max(Mod(acomm(am, dag(am)) - diag(4)), Mod(acomm(bm, dag(bm)) - diag(4)),
             Mod(acomm(am, bm)), Mod(acomm(am, dag(bm))))
  Np <- (dag(a) %*% a + dag(b) %*% b) / 2; Nm <- (dag(am) %*% am + dag(bm) %*% bm) / 2
  Q <- (Np + Nm) / 2
  form <- max(Mod(Nm - ((1 - 2 * P) * Np + P * diag(4) + cc * ss * (dag(a) %*% dag(b) + b %*% a))))
  ev <- sort(eigen(Q, symmetric = TRUE)$values)
  even <- Q[c(1, 4), c(1, 4)]
  qblock <- max(abs(abs(even) - matrix(c(P / 2, cc * ss / 2, cc * ss / 2, 1 - P / 2), 2)))
  v0 <- eigen(Q, symmetric = TRUE)$vectors[, 4]
  sat <- max(abs(c(t(v0) %*% Np %*% v0, t(v0) %*% Nm %*% v0) - ns))
  ## random density matrices, mixed with an eigenvector of N+ - N- so that <N+> = <N->
  D <- Np - Nm; eD <- eigen(D, symmetric = TRUE)
  low <- Inf
  for (k in 1:2000) {
    X <- matrix(rnorm(16), 4) + 1i * matrix(rnorm(16), 4); rho <- X %*% dag(X); rho <- rho / Re(sum(diag(rho)))
    d <- Re(sum(diag(rho %*% D)))
    u <- if (d > 0) eD$vectors[, 4] else eD$vectors[, 1]; du <- Re(sum(Conj(u) * (D %*% u)))
    lam <- d / (d - du); rho <- (1 - lam) * rho + lam * outer(u, Conj(u))
    low <- min(low, Re(sum(diag(rho %*% Np))) - ns)
  }
  vac <- c(1, 0, 0, 0)
  vac_below <- vac_below && (sum(vac * (Np %*% vac)) < ns)
  worst <- pmax(worst, c(car, form, max(abs(ev - c(ns, 0.5, 0.5, 1 - ns))),
                         max(abs(sum(diag(even)) - 1), abs(det(even) - P / 4)), sat, max(0, -low), qblock))
}
## both helicities of one momentum pair: four modes, sixteen states
worst16 <- c(min_eig = 0, sp = 0, sm = 0, vacs = 0); helicity_below <- TRUE
for (P in c(0.2, 0.5, 0.8)) {
  cc <- sqrt(1 - P); ss <- sqrt(P); ns <- (1 - sqrt(1 - P)) / 2
  A1 <- jw(0, 4); B1 <- jw(1, 4); A2 <- jw(2, 4); B2 <- jw(3, 4)
  sector <- function(a, b) { am <- cc * a + ss * dag(b); bm <- cc * b - ss * dag(a)
    list(Np = (dag(a) %*% a + dag(b) %*% b) / 2, Nm = (dag(am) %*% am + dag(bm) %*% bm) / 2, am = am, bm = bm) }
  s1 <- sector(A1, B1); s2 <- sector(A2, B2)
  Qsum <- (s1$Np + s1$Nm + s2$Np + s2$Nm) / 2
  me <- min(eigen(Qsum, symmetric = TRUE)$values)
  ## after-vacuum in helicity h, before-vacuum (c - s A2^dag B2^dag)|0> in helicity -h
  psi <- (cc * diag(16) - ss * dag(A2) %*% dag(B2))[, 1]
  ex <- function(O) Re(sum(Conj(psi) * (O %*% psi)))
  vacs <- max(Mod(s2$am %*% psi), Mod(s2$bm %*% psi), Mod(A1 %*% psi), Mod(B1 %*% psi))
  worst16 <- pmax(worst16, c(abs(me - 2 * ns), abs(ex(s1$Np + s2$Np) - P), abs(ex(s1$Nm + s2$Nm) - P), vacs))
  helicity_below <- helicity_below && ex(s1$Np) < ns - 1e-6
}

chk("lem-1", "lem", "anticommutation relations of a_-, b_- (largest error)", worst[["car"]], 0, tol = 1e-14, label = "0",
    quote = r"(the anticommutation relations hold to $10^{-14}$)", where = "Appendix A")
chk("lem-2", "lem", "N_- = (1-2P) N_+ + P + cs(a^dag b^dag + b a) (largest error)", worst[["formula"]], 0, tol = 1e-13,
    label = "0", quote = r"(N_-=(1-2P)\,N_++P+cs\,\bigl(a_+^\dagger b_+^\dagger+b_+a_+\bigr))", where = "Section 4.1")
chk("lem-3", "lem", "even block of Q: trace 1 and determinant P/4 (largest error)", worst[["block"]], 0, tol = 1e-13,
    label = "0", quote = r"(with trace 1 and determinant $P/4$)", where = "Section 4.1")
chk("lem-3b", "lem", "even block of Q against [[P/2, cs/2], [cs/2, 1 - P/2]] (largest error, off-diagonal in modulus)",
    worst[["qblock"]], 0, tol = 1e-13, label = "0",
    quote = r"(Q=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}P/2&cs/2\\cs/2&1-P/2\end{smallmatrix}\bigr))", where = "Section 4.1")
chk("lem-4", "lem", "eigenvalues of Q against {n_*, 1/2, 1/2, 1 - n_*} (largest error)", worst[["eig"]], 0,
    tol = 1e-13, label = "0", quote = r"(Q\ \text{has eigenvalues}\ \{n_*,\tfrac12,\tfrac12,1-n_*\})", where = "Section 4.1")
chk("lem-5", "lem", "eigenvector at n_*: <N+> = <N-> = n_* (largest error)", worst[["saturate"]], 0, tol = 1e-12,
    label = "0", quote = r"(the eigenvector at $n_*$ has $\langle N_+\rangle=\langle N_-\rangle=n_*$)", where = "Appendix A")
chk("lem-6", "lem", "2000 random states per P with <N+> = <N->: depth below n_*", worst[["below"]], 0, tol = 1e-12,
    label = "0", quote = r"(Q\succeq n_*\,\mathbf 1)", where = "Section 4.1")
chk("lem-7", "lem", "the after-vacuum, not invariant, sits below n_* (1 = yes)", as.numeric(vac_below), 1, tol = 0,
    label = "1", quote = r"(the vacuum of the after-region, which is not invariant, sits below $n_*$)", where = "Appendix A")
chk("lem-8", "lem", "16 states: least eigenvalue of Q(h) + Q(-h) minus 2 n_*", worst16[["min_eig"]], 0, tol = 1e-12,
    label = "0", quote = r"($Q^{(h)}+Q^{(-h)}$ has least eigenvalue $2n_*$)", where = "Appendix A")
chk("lem-9", "lem", "after-vacuum in h, before-vacuum in -h: |<S+> - P| and |<S-> - P|",
    max(worst16[["sp"]], worst16[["sm"]]), 0, tol = 1e-12, label = "0",
    quote = r"(has $\langle S_+\rangle=\langle S_-\rangle=P\ge2n_*$)", where = "Appendix A")
chk("lem-10", "lem", "that state is annihilated by a_+, b_+ (h) and a_-, b_- (-h) (largest residual)",
    worst16[["vacs"]], 0, tol = 1e-12, label = "0", where = "construction")
chk("lem-11", "lem", "its first helicity alone sits below n_* (1 = yes)", as.numeric(helicity_below), 1, tol = 0,
    label = "1", quote = r"(while its first helicity alone sits below $n_*$)", where = "Appendix A")
show_checks("lem")
```

# No floor

Section 4.3 and Table A.1: a state at the upper edge of the family, $n=1-n_*$, below $x_c$ and at
the half-angle state above. The rows of Table A.1 sit at $x_c=k/\sqrt\pi$ with
$k=0.25,0.5,0.75,1,1.5,2,3$, Boyle, Finn and Turok's variable $\sqrt\pi\,x$; the printed $x_c$ are
these values to three decimals, and the integrals below use the unrounded ones.

```{r no-floor}
I_state <- function(xc) {
  lo <- if (xc > 0) integrate(function(x) x^2 * (1 - n_star(x)), 0, xc, rel.tol = 1e-12)$value else 0
  hi <- integrate(function(x) x^2 * n_star(x), xc, Inf, rel.tol = 1e-12)$value
  (lo + hi) / sqrt(pi)
}
tabA1 <- data.frame(k = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3),
                    xc_p = c("0.141", "0.282", "0.423", "0.564", "0.846", "1.128", "1.693"),
                    r_p = c("1.008", "1.119", "1.574", "2.700", "8.312", "20.256", "70.467"),
                    M_p = c("490.1", "470.0", "410.0", "330.4", "210.7", "147.6", "89.6"))
tabA1$xc <- tabA1$k / sqrt(pi)
tabA1$ratio <- vapply(tabA1$xc, I_state, 0) / I_star_cf
tabA1$M <- M_star * tabA1$ratio^-0.4 / 1e6
for (i in seq_len(nrow(tabA1))) {
  row <- with(tabA1[i, ], sprintf("| %s | %s | %s |", xc_p, r_p, M_p))
  chk(sprintf("floor-%da", i), "floor", sprintf("x_c = %.2f / sqrt(pi)", tabA1$k[i]), tabA1$xc[i], tabA1$xc_p[i],
      quote = row, where = "Table A.1")
  chk(sprintf("floor-%db", i), "floor", sprintf("I/I_* at x_c = %.4f", tabA1$xc[i]), tabA1$ratio[i], tabA1$r_p[i],
      quote = row, where = "Table A.1")
  chk(sprintf("floor-%dc", i), "floor", sprintf("M at x_c = %.4f, PeV", tabA1$xc[i]), tabA1$M[i], tabA1$M_p[i],
      quote = row, where = "Table A.1")
}
chk("floor-8", "floor", "M at x_c = 1/sqrt(pi), PeV (text)", tabA1$M[4], "330.4",
    quote = r"(gives 330.4 PeV at $x_c=0.564$, 89.6 PeV at $x_c=1.693$)", where = "Section 4.3")
chk("floor-9", "floor", "M at x_c = 3/sqrt(pi), PeV (text)", tabA1$M[7], "89.6",
    quote = r"(gives 330.4 PeV at $x_c=0.564$, 89.6 PeV at $x_c=1.693$)", where = "Section 4.3")
show_checks("floor")
```

# Helicity sums

Appendix B: an $s$-channel graviton with $\mathcal L=-h_{\mu\nu}T^{\mu\nu}/M_P$ and the de Donder
propagator gives $\mathcal M=[T_i^{\mu\nu}T_{f\,\mu\nu}-\tfrac12T_iT_f]/(M_P^2s)$. The stress-tensor
matrix elements come from explicit helicity spinors in the chiral basis and from helicity
polarisation vectors; nothing is traced. The tools are checked first: the Clifford algebra, the
massless Dirac equation, the completeness sums $\sum u\bar u=\sum v\bar v=\not p$, and the helicity
of the spinors.

```{r tools}
cliff <- 0
for (m in 1:4) for (n in 1:4)
  cliff <- max(cliff, Mod(GAM[[m]] %*% GAM[[n]] + GAM[[n]] %*% GAM[[m]] - 2 * ETA[m, n] * diag(4)))
th <- 1.1; ph <- 0.7; E <- 0.8; p <- mom(E, th, ph)
dirac_eq <- max(sapply(c(1, -1), function(h) max(Mod(slash(p) %*% u_sp(E, th, ph, h)), Mod(slash(p) %*% v_sp(E, th, ph, h)))))
compl <- max(Mod(Reduce(`+`, lapply(c(1, -1), function(h) u_sp(E, th, ph, h) %*% dbar(u_sp(E, th, ph, h)))) - slash(p)),
             Mod(Reduce(`+`, lapply(c(1, -1), function(h) v_sp(E, th, ph, h) %*% dbar(v_sp(E, th, ph, h)))) - slash(p)))
Sn <- Reduce(`+`, Map(`*`, SIGMA, nvec(th, ph))); Sig <- blk(Sn, Z2, Z2, Sn)
heli <- max(Mod(Sig %*% u_sp(E, th, ph, 1) - u_sp(E, th, ph, 1)), Mod(Sig %*% u_sp(E, th, ph, -1) + u_sp(E, th, ph, -1)))
chk("tool-1", "tool", "Clifford algebra {g^m, g^n} = 2 eta^mn (largest error)", cliff, 0, tol = 1e-14, label = "0", where = "identity")
chk("tool-2", "tool", "massless Dirac equation for u and v (largest residual)", dirac_eq, 0, tol = 1e-14, label = "0", where = "identity")
chk("tool-3", "tool", "completeness sums equal p-slash (largest error)", compl, 0, tol = 1e-14, label = "0", where = "identity")
chk("tool-4", "tool", "helicity of u: Sigma.n u = h u (largest error)", heli, 0, tol = 1e-14, label = "0", where = "identity")
show_checks("tool")
```

Each channel ends in one Dirac pair, summed over all spins; $c=\cos\theta$ in the centre of mass,
$s=1$.

```{r helicity}
shape <- list(scalar = function(c) c^2 * (1 - c^2) / 8,
              dirac  = function(c) (4 * c^4 - 3 * c^2 + 1) / 16,
              vector = function(c) (1 - c^4) / 4)
cs <- c(-0.9, -0.3, 0.2, 0.7, 0.95)
dev_shape <- sapply(names(shape), function(ch) max(abs(sapply(cs, function(c) spin_sum(ch, "dirac", c)) - shape[[ch]](cs))))
phi_dep <- max(abs(sapply(names(shape), function(ch) spin_sum(ch, "dirac", 0.37, phi = 0.3) - spin_sum(ch, "dirac", 0.37, phi = 2.2))))
## the full matrix of angular integrals: plasma channel (rows) into each kind of dark matter (columns)
DM <- list(scalar0 = c("scalar", 0), scalar16 = c("scalar", 1 / 6), dirac = c("dirac", 0), vector = c("vector", 0))
Kmat <- sapply(DM, function(d) sapply(c("scalar", "dirac", "vector"), function(ch)
  ang_int(function(c) spin_sum(ch, d[[1]], c, xi_out = as.numeric(d[[2]])))))
Kd <- Kmat[, "dirac"]
## forward direction
fwd <- sapply(names(shape), function(ch) spin_sum(ch, "dirac", 1 - 1e-12))
## gauge-boson vertex with a polarisation replaced by its momentum, and the Feynman-gauge sum
E <- 0.5; p1 <- mom(E, 0, 0); p2 <- mom(E, pi, 0)
ward <- max(sapply(final_T("dirac", 0.4), function(Tf) Mod(amp(T_vector(p1, p1, p2, eps_h(pi, 0, 1)), Tf))),
            sapply(final_T("dirac", 0.4), function(Tf) Mod(amp(T_vector(p1, eps_h(0, 0, -1), p2, p2), Tf))))
feyn <- 0
for (Tf in final_T("dirac", 0.4)) {
  A <- matrix(0i, 4, 4)
  for (i in 1:4) for (j in 1:4) A[i, j] <- amp(T_vector(p1, as.vector(ETA[, i]), p2, as.vector(ETA[, j])), Tf)
  feyn <- feyn + Re(sum(A * Conj(A) * outer(diag(ETA), diag(ETA))))
}
feyn_ratio <- feyn / spin_sum("vector", "dirac", 0.4)

q_shapes <- r"(\textstyle\sum|\mathcal M|^2=\tfrac18c^2(1-c^2),\quad\tfrac1{16}(4c^4-3c^2+1),\quad\tfrac14(1-c^4))"
q_ints <- r"(the angular integrals are $\pi/15$, $\pi/5$ and $4\pi/5$)"
chk("hel-1", "hel", "real scalars: largest |sum|M|^2 - c^2(1-c^2)/8| at five angles", dev_shape[["scalar"]], 0, tol = 1e-14, label = "0", quote = q_shapes, where = "Appendix B")
chk("hel-2", "hel", "Dirac pair: largest |sum|M|^2 - (4c^4-3c^2+1)/16|", dev_shape[["dirac"]], 0, tol = 1e-14, label = "0", quote = q_shapes, where = "Appendix B")
chk("hel-3", "hel", "gauge bosons: largest |sum|M|^2 - (1-c^4)/4|", dev_shape[["vector"]], 0, tol = 1e-14, label = "0", quote = q_shapes, where = "Appendix B")
chk("hel-4", "hel", "real scalars: angular integral", Kd[["scalar"]], pi / 15, rel = 1e-10, label = "pi/15", quote = q_ints, where = "Appendix B")
chk("hel-5", "hel", "Dirac pair: angular integral", Kd[["dirac"]], pi / 5, rel = 1e-10, label = "pi/5", quote = q_ints, where = "Appendix B")
chk("hel-6", "hel", "gauge bosons: angular integral", Kd[["vector"]], 4 * pi / 5, rel = 1e-10, label = "4 pi/5", quote = q_ints, where = "Appendix B")
chk("hel-7", "hel", "no dependence on the azimuth (largest difference)", phi_dep, 0, tol = 1e-14, label = "0", where = "identity")
chk("hel-8", "hel", "scalar and gauge channels vanish along the beam (largest value at c = 1)",
    max(fwd[["scalar"]], fwd[["vector"]]), 0, tol = 1e-10, label = "0",
    quote = r"(so the scalar and gauge-boson channels vanish in the forward direction and the fermion channel does not)", where = "Appendix B")
chk("hel-9", "hel", "fermion channel along the beam", fwd[["dirac"]], 1 / 8, rel = 1e-8, label = "1/8 (nonzero)",
    quote = r"(so the scalar and gauge-boson channels vanish in the forward direction and the fermion channel does not)", where = "Appendix B")
chk("hel-10", "hel", "gauge vertex with e -> p, either boson (largest |M|)", ward, 0, tol = 1e-14, label = "0",
    quote = r"(the vertex built from the field strength vanishes when a polarisation is replaced by its momentum)", where = "Appendix B")
chk("hel-11", "hel", "Feynman-gauge sum -eta over physical sum", feyn_ratio, 1, rel = 1e-10, label = "1",
    quote = r"(for it the Feynman-gauge sum $-\eta_{\mu\nu}$ equals the physical one)", where = "Appendix B")
show_checks("hel")
```

# Spin-2 universality

With the factor 1/2 for identical particles, the three angular integrals stand
$\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac\pi{15}:\tfrac\pi5:\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac{4\pi}5=1:6:12$. Because the final pair's
stress tensor is traceless, only the spin-2 part of the propagator acts, so the same ratio must
appear in the widths of a massive spin-2 particle into a real scalar pair, a Dirac pair and a pair
of gauge bosons. The widths are computed here from the same stress tensors, contracted with the
five polarisation tensors of a massive spin-2 particle at rest, and set beside two published sets,
quoted and not derived:

* Han, Lykken and Zhang, hep-ph/9811350 (arXiv v4): Eq. (46) $N\kappa^2m^3/160\pi$ for massless gauge
  bosons; Eq. (49) $\delta\,\kappa^2m^3/80\pi\,(1-4r)^{1/2}(\tfrac{13}{12}+\dots)$ for massive ones, with
  $\delta=1/2$ for identical particles; Eq. (52) $N_c\kappa^2m^3/320\pi$ for a fermion pair; Eq. (53)
  $\kappa^2m^3/960\pi$ for a pair of Higgs bosons, with the scalar coupling written for a complex
  field in their Eq. (34), so that one real scalar pair has half of it;
* Bernal et al., arXiv:1803.01866, Eqs. (21) to (23) (PRD Eqs. A5 to A7): $g^2m^3/960\pi\Lambda^2$ for a
  real scalar pair, $g^2m^3/160\pi\Lambda^2$ for a Dirac pair and $13\,g^2m^3/960\pi\Lambda^2$ for a
  massive vector pair at $r\to0$.

Only ratios are compared, so the normalisation of each paper's coupling drops out.

```{r spin2}
unit3 <- function(i, j) { M <- matrix(0, 3, 3); M[i, j] <- 1; M }
pol3 <- list((unit3(1, 2) + unit3(2, 1)) / sqrt(2), (unit3(1, 3) + unit3(3, 1)) / sqrt(2),
             (unit3(2, 3) + unit3(3, 2)) / sqrt(2), (unit3(1, 1) - unit3(2, 2)) / sqrt(2),
             (unit3(1, 1) + unit3(2, 2) - 2 * unit3(3, 3)) / sqrt(6))
pol4 <- lapply(pol3, function(b) { M <- matrix(0, 4, 4); M[2:4, 2:4] <- b; M })
pol_ok <- max(sapply(seq_along(pol3), function(i) sapply(seq_along(pol3), function(j)
  abs(sum(pol3[[i]] * pol3[[j]]) - (i == j)))))
## |eps_{mu nu} T^{mu nu}|^2 for a decay at rest (mass 1) into the pair along n(theta, phi), summed over the
## final spins and averaged over the five polarisations; the width is S times its angular integral, up to a
## common factor, with S = 1/2 for identical particles
decay_sq <- function(kind, c, phi = 0.4) {
  tot <- 0
  for (e in pol4) for (T in final_T(kind, c, phi)) tot <- tot + Mod(sum((ETA %*% e %*% ETA) * T))^2
  tot / 5
}
Gam <- c(scalar = 0.5, dirac = 1, vector = 0.5) *
       sapply(c("scalar", "dirac", "vector"), function(k) ang_int(function(c) decay_sq(k, c)))
q_univ <- r"(stand $\pi/30:\pi/5:2\pi/5=1:6:12$)"
q_hlz <- r"(stand 12 to 6 to 2 for a gauge-boson pair, a Dirac pair and a complex scalar pair)"
chk("spin2-0", "spin2", "polarisation tensors orthonormal (largest error)", pol_ok, 0, tol = 1e-14, label = "0", where = "identity")
chk("spin2-1", "spin2", "widths: Dirac over real scalar, against the angular integrals", Gam[["dirac"]] / Gam[["scalar"]],
    Kd[["dirac"]] / (Kd[["scalar"]] / 2), rel = 1e-10, label = "6", quote = q_univ, where = "Appendix C")
chk("spin2-2", "spin2", "widths: gauge bosons over real scalar, against the angular integrals", Gam[["vector"]] / Gam[["scalar"]],
    Kd[["vector"]] / Kd[["scalar"]], rel = 1e-10, label = "12", quote = q_univ, where = "Appendix C")
chk("spin2-3", "spin2", "widths: gauge bosons over Dirac, against Han et al. (46)/(52)", Gam[["vector"]] / Gam[["dirac"]],
    (1 / 160) / (1 / 320), rel = 1e-10, label = "2 (quoted)", quote = q_hlz, where = "Appendix C")
chk("spin2-4", "spin2", "widths: complex scalar pair (two real) over Dirac, against Han et al. (53)/(52)",
    2 * Gam[["scalar"]] / Gam[["dirac"]], (1 / 960) / (1 / 320), rel = 1e-10, label = "1/3 (quoted)", quote = q_hlz, where = "Appendix C")
chk("spin2-5", "spin2", "massive vector pair at r -> 0 (gauge bosons plus one real scalar) over gauge bosons, against Han et al. (49)/(46)",
    (Gam[["vector"]] + Gam[["scalar"]]) / Gam[["vector"]], 13 / 12, rel = 1e-10, label = "13/12 (quoted)", where = "literature")
chk("spin2-6", "spin2", "widths: real scalar over Dirac, against Bernal et al. (21)/(22)", Gam[["scalar"]] / Gam[["dirac"]],
    (1 / 960) / (1 / 160), rel = 1e-10, label = "1/6 (quoted)", where = "literature")
chk("spin2-7", "spin2", "massive vector pair at r -> 0 over real scalar, against Bernal et al. (23)/(21)",
    (Gam[["vector"]] + Gam[["scalar"]]) / Gam[["scalar"]], 13, rel = 1e-10, label = "13 (quoted)",
    quote = r"(give 13 in place of 12 for vectors far above their mass)", where = "Appendix C")
chk("spin2-8", "spin2", "the same, for the paper's statement on massive vector dark matter", (Gam[["vector"]] + Gam[["scalar"]]) / Gam[["scalar"]],
    13, rel = 1e-10, label = "12 + 1", quote = r"(one made far above its mass adds a longitudinal mode)", where = "Section 2")
show_checks("spin2")
```

The computed widths stand `r paste(sprintf("%.4g", Gam / Gam[["scalar"]]), collapse = " : ")`, the
ratio of the angular integrals. Han, Lykken and Zhang's Eq. (53) is the width into a complex scalar
pair, two real scalars, since their Eq. (34) writes the scalar's stress tensor for a complex field;
with that reading all four of their widths agree, and so do Bernal et al.'s.

# Thermal integrals

The rate density is
$R=(1024\pi^6)^{-1}\int f_1f_2E_1E_2\,dE_1\,dE_2\,d\cos\theta_{12}\int\sum|\mathcal M|^2d\Omega$, with
$\int\sum|\mathcal M|^2d\Omega=K s^2/M_P^4$ from the helicity sums and $s=2E_1E_2(1-\cos\theta_{12})$,
a factor 1/2 for identical initial bosons, and energies in units of $T$. Each coefficient is done
two ways: the three-dimensional integral by adaptive cubature, and the closed form
$\int_0^\infty E^3f\,dE=\Gamma(4)\zeta(4)$ for bosons and $\tfrac78\Gamma(4)\zeta(4)$ for fermions,
with $\zeta(4)$ summed here, so that the energy and angle integrals give $\tfrac{32}3J_1J_2$.

```{r thermal}
fB <- function(E) 1 / expm1(E); fF <- function(E) 1 / (exp(E) + 1); fMB <- function(E) exp(-E)
z4 <- zeta_num(4); z3 <- zeta_num(3)
moment <- function(f) integrate(function(E) E^3 * f(E), 0, Inf, rel.tol = 1e-12)$value
JB <- 6 * z4; JF <- (7 / 8) * 6 * z4
triple <- function(f, tol = 1e-8) hcubature(function(X) {
  E1 <- X[1, ]; E2 <- X[2, ]; s <- 2 * E1 * E2 * (1 - X[3, ])
  matrix(f(E1) * f(E2) * E1 * E2 * s^2, nrow = 1) }, c(0, 0, -1), c(50, 50, 1), tol = tol,
  vectorInterface = TRUE)$integral
W <- c(B = triple(fB), F = triple(fF), MB = triple(fMB))
w_ch <- c(scalar = 0.5, dirac = 1, vector = 0.5)       # identical initial bosons; a Dirac pair is not
per_num <- w_ch * Kd * W[c("B", "F", "B")] / (1024 * pi^6)
per <- w_ch * Kd * (32 / 3) * c(JB, JF, JB)^2 / (1024 * pi^6)
names(per_num) <- names(per) <- names(w_ch)
N_SM <- c(scalar = 4, dirac = 22.5, vector = 12)        # 45 Weyl fermions count as 22.5 Dirac
alpha_num <- sum(N_SM * per_num)
alpha <- sum(N_SM * per)
alpha_exact <- pi^3 * (1 / 162000 + 49 / 307200 + 1 / 4500)
alpha_sec4 <- pi^3 * (4 / 648000 + 49 * 45 / 13824000 + 12 / 54000)
alpha47 <- sum(c(4, 23.5, 12) * per)

q_per <- r"(give $\pi^3/648000$ per real scalar, $49\pi^3/6912000$ per Dirac fermion and $\pi^3/54000$ per gauge boson)"
chk("therm-1", "therm", "zeta(4) by summation against pi^4/90", z4, pi^4 / 90, rel = 1e-13, label = "pi^4/90", where = "closed form")
chk("therm-2", "therm", "Int E^3/(e^E - 1) dE by quadrature", moment(fB), JB, rel = 1e-10, label = "6 zeta(4) = pi^4/15", where = "closed form")
chk("therm-3", "therm", "Int E^3/(e^E + 1) dE by quadrature", moment(fF), JF, rel = 1e-10, label = "(7/8) 6 zeta(4) = 7 pi^4/120", where = "closed form")
chk("therm-4", "therm", "per real scalar, cubature", per_num[["scalar"]], pi^3 / 648000, rel = 1e-7, label = "pi^3/648000", quote = q_per, where = "Appendix B")
chk("therm-5", "therm", "per Dirac fermion, cubature", per_num[["dirac"]], 49 * pi^3 / 6912000, rel = 1e-7, label = "49 pi^3/6912000", quote = q_per, where = "Appendix B")
chk("therm-6", "therm", "per gauge boson, cubature", per_num[["vector"]], pi^3 / 54000, rel = 1e-7, label = "pi^3/54000", quote = q_per, where = "Appendix B")
chk("therm-7", "therm", "per real scalar, closed form", per[["scalar"]], pi^3 / 648000, rel = 1e-12, label = "pi^3/648000", quote = q_per, where = "Appendix B")
chk("therm-8", "therm", "per Dirac fermion, closed form", per[["dirac"]], 49 * pi^3 / 6912000, rel = 1e-12, label = "49 pi^3/6912000", quote = q_per, where = "Appendix B")
chk("therm-9", "therm", "per gauge boson, closed form", per[["vector"]], pi^3 / 54000, rel = 1e-12, label = "pi^3/54000", quote = q_per, where = "Appendix B")
chk("therm-10", "therm", "alpha (4, 22.5 Dirac, 12) by cubature", alpha_num, alpha_exact, rel = 1e-7,
    label = "pi^3(1/162000 + 49/307200 + 1/4500)", quote = r"(\alpha=\pi^3\Bigl(\frac{1}{162000}+\frac{49}{307200}+\frac1{4500}\Bigr))", where = "Appendix B")
chk("therm-11", "therm", "alpha, closed form", alpha, "1.2027e-2",
    quote = r"(\frac{49}{307200}+\frac1{4500}\Bigr)=1.2027\times10^{-2})", where = "Appendix B")
chk("therm-12", "therm", "alpha from Section 2's formula with 4, 45 Weyl, 12", alpha_sec4, "1.20e-2",
    quote = r"(\frac{N_{\rm s}}{648000}+\frac{49\,N_{\rm f}}{13824000}+\frac{N_{\rm v}}{54000}\Bigr)=1.20\times10^{-2})", where = "Section 2")
chk("therm-13", "therm", "the two forms of alpha agree", alpha_sec4, alpha, rel = 1e-12, label = "alpha above", where = "identity")
chk("therm-14", "therm", "47 Weyl fermions (N2, N3 in the plasma): rise of alpha, per cent", 100 * (alpha47 / alpha - 1), "1.8",
    quote = r"(47 Weyl fermions enter and $\alpha$ rises by 1.8 per cent)", where = "Section 5")
show_checks("therm")
```

# Rates for other dark matter

Table 1 replaces the final Dirac pair by a real scalar pair with $\xi=0$ or $1/6$ (improvement term
$-2\xi(P^\mu P^\nu-\eta^{\mu\nu}P^2)$ in the scalar's stress tensor), by a Dirac pair, or by a pair
of massless vectors, keeps the plasma's scalars minimally coupled, and puts 1/2 in the event rate
for identical final particles. Per Weyl fermion of the plasma the weight is half the Dirac spin sum.
The angular integrals, in units of π, are:

```{r table1-K}
Kfrac <- apply(Kmat / pi, c(1, 2), as_fraction)
html_table(data.frame(`plasma pair` = c("real scalars", "Dirac pair", "gauge bosons"), Kfrac, check.names = FALSE),
           col.names = c("plasma pair", "real scalar, xi = 0", "real scalar, xi = 1/6", "Dirac pair", "massless vectors"))
```

```{r table1}
ident <- c(scalar0 = 0.5, scalar16 = 0.5, dirac = 1, vector = 0.5)       # identical final particles
w_in <- c(scalar = 0.5, dirac = 0.5, vector = 0.5)  # identical initial bosons; per Weyl, half a Dirac sum
Jin <- c(scalar = JB, dirac = JF, vector = JB)
rtab <- sapply(names(DM), function(d) ident[[d]] * w_in * Kmat[, d] * (32 / 3) * Jin^2 / (1024 * pi^6) / pi^3)
R_SM <- apply(rtab, 2, function(r) pi^3 * sum(c(4, 45, 12) * r))
R_45 <- apply(rtab, 2, function(r) pi^3 * sum(c(4, 90, 12) * r))
paper_t1 <- list(
  scalar0  = list(r = c(1 / 648000, 49 / 82944000, 1 / 324000), lab = c("1/648000", "49/82944000", "1/324000"), R = "2.16e-3", x = "1.38",
                  row = r"(| real scalar, $\xi=0$ | $\pi^3/648000$ | $49\pi^3/82944000$ | $\pi^3/324000$ | $2.16\times10^{-3}$ | 1.38 |)"),
  scalar16 = list(r = c(1 / 3888000, 49 / 82944000, 1 / 324000), lab = c("1/3888000", "49/82944000", "1/324000"), R = "2.00e-3", x = "1.41",
                  row = r"(| real scalar, $\xi=1/6$ | $\pi^3/3888000$ | $49\pi^3/82944000$ | $\pi^3/324000$ | $2.00\times10^{-3}$ | 1.41 |)"),
  dirac    = list(r = c(1 / 648000, 49 / 13824000, 1 / 54000), lab = c("1/648000", "49/13824000", "1/54000"), R = "1.20e-2", x = "1.41",
                  row = r"(| Dirac fermion | $\pi^3/648000$ | $49\pi^3/13824000$ | $\pi^3/54000$ | $1.20\times10^{-2}$ | 1.41 |)"),
  vector   = list(r = c(1 / 324000, 49 / 6912000, 1 / 27000), lab = c("1/324000", "49/6912000", "1/27000"), R = "2.41e-2", x = "1.41",
                  row = r"(| massless vector | $\pi^3/324000$ | $49\pi^3/6912000$ | $\pi^3/27000$ | $2.41\times10^{-2}$ | 1.41 |)"))
cols <- c("per real scalar", "per Weyl fermion", "per gauge boson")
dm_name <- c(scalar0 = "real scalar, xi = 0", scalar16 = "real scalar, xi = 1/6", dirac = "Dirac fermion",
             vector = "massless vector")
for (d in names(DM)) {
  pt <- paper_t1[[d]]
  for (j in 1:3) chk(sprintf("tab1-%s-%d", d, j), "tab1", sprintf("%s: %s (units pi^3), = %s", dm_name[[d]], cols[j],
                     as_fraction(rtab[j, d])), rtab[j, d], pt$r[j], rel = 1e-10, label = pt$lab[j], quote = pt$row, where = "Table 1")

      quote = pt$row, where = "Table 1")
}
## xi enters only the channel with plasma scalars; fermion and gauge stress tensors are traceless
xi_only <- max(abs(Kmat["dirac", "scalar0"] - Kmat["dirac", "scalar16"]), abs(Kmat["vector", "scalar0"] - Kmat["vector", "scalar16"]))
tr_f <- max(sapply(final_T("dirac", 0.3), function(T) Mod(trT(T))), sapply(final_T("vector", 0.3), function(T) Mod(trT(T))))
```
