# Double count in published rates

Counting 45 Dirac fermions in place of 22.5 gives the sums that Clery et al. and Bernal et al.
print. Their printed coefficients are quoted from the papers: Clery et al., PRD 105 (2022) 075005,
Eqs. (A8) and (A12), $3997\pi^3/20736000$ and $11351\pi^3/10368000$; Bernal et al.,
arXiv:1803.01866, Eq. (41), $11351\pi^3/331776000$ for the massless graviton.

```{r double-count}
S45 <- sum(c(4, 45, 12) * per)
S45_scalar <- R_45[["scalar0"]]
clery_A12 <- 11351 * pi^3 / 10368000; clery_A8 <- 3997 * pi^3 / 20736000; bernal_41 <- 11351 * pi^3 / 331776000
q45 <- r"($11351\pi^3/20736000=1.697\times10^{-2}$ per event, 1.41 times $\alpha$)"
chk("dbl-1", "dbl", "45-Dirac sum against 11351 pi^3/20736000", S45, 11351 * pi^3 / 20736000, rel = 1e-12,
    label = "11351 pi^3/20736000", quote = q45, where = "Section 2")
chk("dbl-2", "dbl", "45-Dirac sum", S45, "1.697e-2", quote = q45, where = "Section 2")
chk("dbl-3", "dbl", "45-Dirac sum over alpha", S45 / alpha, "1.41", quote = q45, where = "Section 2")
chk("dbl-4", "dbl", "Clery et al. Eq. (A12) over the 45-Dirac sum", clery_A12 / S45, 2, rel = 1e-12, label = "2 (exactly twice)",
    quote = r"(and Clery et al.'s Eq. (A12) is exactly twice that)", where = "Section 2")
chk("dbl-5", "dbl", "45-Dirac sum for a minimally coupled scalar", S45_scalar, 3997 * pi^3 / 41472000, rel = 1e-12,
    label = "3997 pi^3/41472000", quote = r"(that sum, $3997\pi^3/41472000$, is 1.38 times the corrected value)", where = "Section 2")
chk("dbl-6", "dbl", "the same over the corrected scalar rate", S45_scalar / R_SM[["scalar0"]], "1.38",
    quote = r"(that sum, $3997\pi^3/41472000$, is 1.38 times the corrected value)", where = "Section 2")
chk("dbl-7", "dbl", "Clery et al. Eq. (A8) over the 45-Dirac scalar sum", clery_A8 / S45_scalar, 2, rel = 1e-12, label = "2",
    quote = r"(is likewise twice our 45-Dirac sum)", where = "Section 2")
chk("dbl-8", "dbl", "abundance factor, fermion dark matter (count alone)", S45 / alpha, "1.41",
    quote = r"(so their thermal abundances are 1.41 times too high for Dirac fermion dark matter and 1.38 times)", where = "Section 2")
chk("dbl-9", "dbl", "abundance factor, minimally coupled scalar", S45_scalar / R_SM[["scalar0"]], "1.38",
    quote = r"(so their thermal abundances are 1.41 times too high for Dirac fermion dark matter and 1.38 times)", where = "Section 2")
chk("dbl-10", "dbl", "Bernal et al.'s coefficient 11351 pi^3/331776000", bernal_41, "1.06e-3",
    quote = r"($11351\pi^3/331776000=1.06\times10^{-3}$, exactly $1/16$ of)", where = "Appendix C")
chk("dbl-11", "dbl", "Bernal et al. over the 45-Dirac sum", bernal_41 / S45, 1 / 16, rel = 1e-12, label = "1/16",
    quote = r"($11351\pi^3/331776000=1.06\times10^{-3}$, exactly $1/16$ of)", where = "Appendix C")
chk("dbl-12", "dbl", "fermion dark matter: highest temperature rises by (45-Dirac/alpha)^(1/3)", (S45 / alpha)^(1 / 3), "1.12",
    quote = r"(by $1.41^{1/3}=1.12$ for fermion dark matter)", where = "Section 2")
show_checks("dbl")
```

Bernal et al.'s Eq. (8) is the weighting $4|M_0|^2+45|M_{1/2}|^2+12|M_1|^2$; the coefficient
$11351\pi^3/331776000$ is their Eq. (41) in the arXiv numbering and Eq. (B17) in the PRD, and their
Table I rounds it to $1.1\times10^{-3}$.

# Einstein limit of Boyle, Turok and Vaibhav

Their rate is rebuilt from what they print in Appendix E of arXiv:2609.11750: (E1)
$\dot n=2\sum_in_i^2\langle\sigma v\rangle_i$; (E2) $n_i=\xi_i\zeta(3)T^3/\pi^2$ with $\xi_i=1$ for
bosons and 3/4 for fermions; (E24) $\langle\sigma v\rangle_i=24A_iT^2/M_P^4$ with (E22)
$A=4,3,29$ in units of $1/3840\pi$ for spin 0, 1/2 and 1; (E12) 4 scalar states, 94 fermion
states and 24 vector states, $g_{*n}=98.5$; and (E27b) $C_{\rm IR}=1393/(25216\pi^3)\approx2.1\times10^{-3}$.
Their $M_{\rm pl}=(8\pi G)^{-1/2}$ is the reduced Planck mass. The same $A$ follow from the helicity
sums here, $A=60K/(\pi n_{\rm init})$ with $n_{\rm init}$ the initial spin states averaged over.

```{r btv}
A_ours <- 60 * Kd / (pi * c(1, 4, 4))
btv <- function(A = c(4, 3, 29), pair = 2, scalar_half = 1, nf = 94, stats = "quantum") {
  n2 <- if (stats == "quantum") c(1, 9 / 16, 1) * (z3 / pi^2)^2 else rep(1 / pi^4, 3)
  pair * 24 * sum(c(4 * scalar_half, nf, 24) * n2 * A) / (3840 * pi)
}
b0 <- btv(); b1 <- btv(A = A_ours); b2 <- btv(A = A_ours, pair = 1); b3 <- btv(A = A_ours, pair = 1, scalar_half = 0.5)
ours_mb <- sum(N_SM * w_ch * Kd * W[["MB"]] / (1024 * pi^6))
btv_mb <- btv(A = A_ours, pair = 1, scalar_half = 0.5, stats = "MB")
btv_mb45 <- btv(A = A_ours, pair = 1, scalar_half = 0.5, stats = "MB", nf = 90)
ours_mb_cf <- sum(N_SM * w_ch * Kd * (32 / 3) * 36 / (1024 * pi^6))      # Int E^3 e^-E dE = 6
C_IR <- b0 / (2 * 98.5 * z3 / pi^2)
C_IR_printed <- 1393 / (25216 * pi^3)
row <- function(a, b, c) sprintf("| %s | %s | %s |", a, b, c)
chk("btv-1", "btv", "A from the helicity sums, spin 0, units 1/(3840 pi)", A_ours[[1]], 4, rel = 1e-10, label = "4 (theirs)", where = "their (E22)")
chk("btv-2", "btv", "A from the helicity sums, spin 1/2", A_ours[[2]], 3, rel = 1e-10, label = "3 (theirs)", where = "their (E22)")
chk("btv-3", "btv", "their spin-1 A over the one from the helicity sums", 29 / A_ours[[3]], 29 / 12, rel = 1e-10, label = "29/12",
    quote = r"(Their gauge-boson cross-section is 29/12 of ours)", where = "Appendix B")
chk("btv-4", "btv", "as printed", b0, "5.14e-2", quote = row("as printed", r"($5.14\times10^{-2}$)", "4.27"), where = "Table B.1")
chk("btv-5", "btv", "as printed, over alpha", b0 / alpha, "4.27", quote = row("as printed", r"($5.14\times10^{-2}$)", "4.27"), where = "Table B.1")
chk("btv-6", "btv", "transverse gauge-boson vertex", b1, "2.73e-2", quote = row("transverse gauge-boson vertex", r"($2.73\times10^{-2}$)", "2.27"), where = "Table B.1")
chk("btv-7", "btv", "the same over alpha", b1 / alpha, "2.27", quote = row("transverse gauge-boson vertex", r"($2.73\times10^{-2}$)", "2.27"), where = "Table B.1")
chk("btv-8", "btv", "one Majorana N1 per Dirac-pair event", b2, "1.37e-2", quote = row(r"(one Majorana $N_1$ per Dirac-pair event)", r"($1.37\times10^{-2}$)", "1.135"), where = "Table B.1")
chk("btv-9", "btv", "the same over alpha", b2 / alpha, "1.135", quote = row(r"(one Majorana $N_1$ per Dirac-pair event)", r"($1.37\times10^{-2}$)", "1.135"), where = "Table B.1")
chk("btv-10", "btv", "1/2 for identical real scalars", b3, "1.34e-2", quote = row(r"($1/2$ for identical real scalars)", r"($1.34\times10^{-2}$)", "1.115"), where = "Table B.1")
chk("btv-11", "btv", "the same over alpha", b3 / alpha, "1.115", quote = row(r"($1/2$ for identical real scalars)", r"($1.34\times10^{-2}$)", "1.115"), where = "Table B.1")
chk("btv-12", "btv", "alpha, Bose-Einstein and Fermi-Dirac", alpha, "1.20e-2", quote = row("ours, Bose-Einstein and Fermi-Dirac", r"($1.20\times10^{-2}$)", "1"), where = "Table B.1")
chk("btv-13", "btv", "Maxwell-Boltzmann throughout: theirs, corrected", btv_mb, "1.1805e-2",
    quote = row("both in Maxwell-Boltzmann statistics", r"($1.1805$ against $1.1560\times10^{-2}$)", "1.021"), where = "Table B.1")
chk("btv-14", "btv", "Maxwell-Boltzmann throughout: alpha", ours_mb, "1.1560e-2",
    quote = row("both in Maxwell-Boltzmann statistics", r"($1.1805$ against $1.1560\times10^{-2}$)", "1.021"), where = "Table B.1")
chk("btv-15", "btv", "theirs over alpha, both in Maxwell-Boltzmann statistics", btv_mb / ours_mb, "1.021",
    quote = row("both in Maxwell-Boltzmann statistics", r"($1.1805$ against $1.1560\times10^{-2}$)", "1.021"), where = "Table B.1")
chk("btv-16", "btv", "with 45 Weyl fermions (90 states) in their bath, over alpha (closed form, Maxwell-Boltzmann)", btv_mb45 / ours_mb_cf, 1, rel = 1e-12, label = "1 (agree exactly)",
    quote = r"(With equal species they agree exactly.)", where = "Appendix B")
chk("btv-17", "btv", "factor from the gauge-boson vertex", b0 / b1, "1.88", quote = r"(gives a factor 1.88)", where = "Section 2")
chk("btv-18", "btv", "factor from two N1 per Dirac-pair event", b1 / b2, 2, rel = 1e-12, label = "2",
    quote = r"(counting two $N_1$ per Dirac-pair event gives 2)", where = "Section 2")
chk("btv-19", "btv", "remaining factor (scalar 1/2 and statistics)", b2 / alpha, "1.135", quote = r"(the remaining 1.135 is 1.018 from the missing)", where = "Section 2")
chk("btv-20", "btv", "C_IR from their rate equation", C_IR, "2.1e-3", quote = r"($C_{\rm IR}\approx2.1\times10^{-3}$)", where = "Appendix B")
chk("btv-21", "btv", "their printed closed form 1393/(25216 pi^3)", C_IR_printed, "1.78e-3",
    quote = r"($1393/(25216\pi^3)=1.78\times10^{-3}$, lacks a factor $\zeta(3)$)", where = "Appendix B")
chk("btv-22", "btv", "C_IR over the printed closed form", C_IR / C_IR_printed, z3, rel = 1e-10, label = "zeta(3)",
    quote = r"($1393/(25216\pi^3)=1.78\times10^{-3}$, lacks a factor $\zeta(3)$)", where = "Appendix B")
## their contracted gauge-boson vertex as printed, Eq. (D3), lower indices, with a_(g b_d) read either as
## (a_g b_d + a_d b_g)/2 or as a_g b_d + a_d b_g; e1 for the boson of momentum p, e2 for the one of momentum q
btv_vertex <- function(p, e1, q, e2, half = TRUE) {
  lo <- function(v) as.vector(ETA %*% v)
  sym <- function(a, b) (if (half) 0.5 else 1) * (outer(lo(a), lo(b)) + outer(lo(b), lo(a)))
  V <- 0.5 * (mdot(e1, e2) * (ETA * mdot(p, q) - sym(p, q)) - mdot(e1, q) * mdot(e2, p) * ETA -
              2 * mdot(p, q) * sym(e1, e2) + mdot(e1, q) * sym(e2, p) + mdot(e2, p) * sym(e1, q))
  ETA %*% V %*% ETA                                  # upper indices, to contract with T_f
}
btv_ward <- sapply(c(TRUE, FALSE), function(h) max(sapply(final_T("dirac", 0.4), function(Tf)
  Mod(amp(btv_vertex(p1, p1, p2, eps_h(pi, 0, 1), half = h), Tf)))))
btv_phys <- max(sapply(final_T("dirac", 0.4), function(Tf) Mod(amp(btv_vertex(p1, eps_h(0, 0, 1), p2, eps_h(pi, 0, -1)), Tf))))
## their (D4) and (D5): Int (f2^4/512)(15 + 5c^2 - 6c^4) dOmega / (64 pi^2 s), in units f2^4/(3840 pi s)
D4_int <- integrate(function(c) 15 + 5 * c^2 - 6 * c^4, -1, 1, rel.tol = 1e-13)$value
D5_from_D4 <- 2 * pi * D4_int / 512 / (64 * pi^2) * 3840 * pi
chk("btv-28", "btv", "their vertex (D3), (a b + b a)/2, with e -> p: |M| above 1e-6 (1 = yes)", as.numeric(btv_ward[1] > 1e-6), 1,
    tol = 0, label = "1", quote = r"(when the polarisation $\xi$ is replaced by the photon's momentum $p$)", where = "Appendix B")
chk("btv-29", "btv", "the same with a b + b a (1 = yes)", as.numeric(btv_ward[2] > 1e-6), 1, tol = 0, label = "1",
    quote = r"(when the polarisation $\xi$ is replaced by the photon's momentum $p$)", where = "Appendix B")
chk("btv-30", "btv", "their (D4) integrated over angle, in units f2^4/(3840 pi s), against their (D5)", D5_from_D4, 29 / 4,
    rel = 1e-10, label = "29/4 (their D5)", where = "their (D4), (D5)")
chk("btv-31", "btv", "their angular shape 15 + 5c^2 - 6c^4 along the beam, c = 1", 15 + 5 - 6, 14, tol = 0, label = "14 (nonzero)",
    quote = r"($15+5\cos^2\theta-6\cos^4\theta$, does not vanish along the beam)", where = "Appendix B")
show_checks("btv")
```

With a physical polarisation their vertex gives amplitudes of size `r tex_sci(btv_phys, 2)` here, and
with a polarisation replaced by its momentum `r tex_sci(btv_ward[1], 2)` and `r tex_sci(btv_ward[2], 2)`
for the two readings of the symmetrisation, where the vertex built from field strengths gives zero.

Their yield, from their Eqs. (6), (8) and (11), is proportional to $\Gamma/H$ at
$T_*=(C_{\rm UV}/C_{\rm IR})^{1/4}f_2M_{\rm pl}$, that is to $C_{\rm IR}^{1/4}C_{\rm UV}^{3/4}f_2^3$. The
bound therefore moves as the rate to the power $-1/3$ only if their quadratic-gravity rate $C_{\rm UV}$
changes by the same factor as the Einstein limit. Their $A^{\rm UV}_i=A^{\rm IR}_i/4$ species by
species (Eqs. E17, E22), so the vertex and the two counting corrections carry over unchanged. The
statistics do not: with $\sigma\propto1/s$ the thermal rate takes the first moment
$\int_0^\infty Ef\,dE$ ($\zeta(2)$ for bosons, $\zeta(2)/2$ for fermions) in place of the third.
The same corrections, applied to their UV rate with Bose-Einstein and Fermi-Dirac statistics, give:

```{r btv-uv}
J1 <- c(B = integrate(function(E) E * fB(E), 0, Inf, rel.tol = 1e-12)$value,
        F = integrate(function(E) E * fF(E), 0, Inf, rel.tol = 1e-12)$value)
chk("btv-27", "btv", "Int E/(e^E - 1) dE and Int E/(e^E + 1) dE against zeta(2) and zeta(2)/2 (largest relative error)",
    max(abs(J1 / c(zeta_num(2), zeta_num(2) / 2) - 1)), 0, tol = 1e-10, label = "0", where = "closed form")
## printed rate over the corrected one, per unit of the common factors: states x weight x A x statistics
lam <- function(stat_true) 2 * sum(c(4, 94, 24) * c(1, 9 / 16, 1) * z3^2 * c(4, 3, 29)) /
                           sum(c(4 * 0.5, 90, 24) * c(4, 3, 12) * stat_true)
lam_IR <- lam(c(JB, JF, JB)^2 / 36)                  # MB third moment Gamma(4) = 6
lam_UV <- lam(c(J1[["B"]], J1[["F"]], J1[["B"]])^2)  # MB first moment Gamma(2) = 1
uv <- data.frame(
  case = c("both coefficients moved by the Einstein-limit factor", "Einstein limit alone corrected",
           "C_UV corrected with its own statistics (the paper's reading)"),
  `yield factor` = c(lam_IR, lam_IR^0.25, lam_IR^0.25 * lam_UV^0.75), check.names = FALSE)
uv$`bound factor` <- uv$`yield factor`^(1 / 3)
uv$`f2 bound` <- K("f2_BTV") * uv$`bound factor`
uv$`f2 at a one per cent share` <- 0.01^(1 / 3) * uv$`f2 bound`
chk("btv-26", "btv", "Einstein-limit factor from the species sums (same as b0/alpha)", lam_IR, b0 / alpha, rel = 1e-10,
    label = "b0/alpha", where = "identity")
chk("btv-23", "btv", "their rate above T* over the corrected one (first moments)", lam_UV, "2.56",
    quote = r"(lower $C_{\rm UV}$ by 2.56)", where = "Section 2")
chk("btv-24", "btv", "their f2 bound 7e-5 with both coefficients corrected", uv[["f2 bound"]][3], "1.0e-4",
    quote = r"(coefficients to $1.0\times10^{-4}$; it keeps)", where = "Section 2")
chk("btv-25", "btv", "plasma's share (f2/bound)^3 at one per cent: f2", uv[["f2 at a one per cent share"]][3], "2.15e-5",
    quote = r"(falls under one per cent for $f_2<2.15\times10^{-5}$)", where = "Section 2")
chk("btv-32", "btv", "the same bound in the conclusions", uv[["f2 bound"]][3], "1.0e-4",
    quote = r"(with the Weyl coupling well below $1.0\times10^{-4}$)", where = "Section 7")
html_table(data.frame(lapply(uv, function(v) if (is.numeric(v)) vapply(v, fmt, "", d = 4) else v), check.names = FALSE))
```

The UV rate as printed is `r sprintf("%.2f", lam_UV)` times the corrected one, against
`r sprintf("%.2f", lam_IR)` in the Einstein limit, which puts the bound at
`r tex_sci(uv[["f2 bound"]][3], 2)`, the value Section 2 gives. This rests on their UV formulas
(E16) to (E20) as printed. Moving both coefficients by the Einstein-limit factor alone would give
`r tex_sci(uv[["f2 bound"]][1], 2)`.

# Published rates, channel by channel

Appendix C sets each published rate for fermion dark matter beside the paper's, channel by
channel. The squared amplitudes are read from the papers in the massless limit, with $s=1$,
$t=-(1-c)/2$ and units of $1/M_P^4$:

* Garny et al., JCAP 02 (2018) 027, Eqs. (3.14) to (3.16), with $m_X$ the dark-matter mass and
  $G=m_p^{-2}$, so that $8\pi G=1/M_P^2$ and $G^2\pi^2=1/(64M_P^4)$; the journal text, whose
  equations pdftotext damages, was rebuilt by hand as
  (3.14) $8G^2\pi^2\,(m_X^2-t)(-m_X^2+s+t)(-2m_X^2+s+2t)^2/s^2$,
  (3.15) $(8G^2\pi^2/s^2)\,[32m_X^8-32m_X^6(s+4t)+2m_X^4(5s^2+64st+96t^2)-4m_X^2(s^3+13s^2t+40st^2+32t^3)+s^4+10s^3t+42s^2t^2+64st^3+32t^4]$ and
  (3.16) $-32G^2\pi^2\,(m_X^4-2m_X^2t+t(s+t))\,[s^2+2(m_X^4-2m_X^2t+t(s+t))]/s^2$,
  used at $m_X=0$; their cross-section, Eq. (3.3), integrates over all angles with no factor 1/2,
  and Eq. (3.1) weights the fermion channel by 45;
* Bernal et al., arXiv:1803.01866, Eqs. (35) to (37) (PRD Eqs. B11 to B13):
  $(-t(s+t))(s+2t)^2/32s^2$, $(s^4+10s^3t+42s^2t^2+64st^3+32t^4)/128s^2$ and
  $(-t(s+t))(s^2+2t(s+t))/8s^2$; their rate is Eq. (41) (PRD Eq. B17);
* Clery et al., PRD 105 (2022) 075005, Eqs. (A9) to (A11), which include the symmetry factors:
  $(-t(s+t))(s+2t)^2/4s^2$, $(s^4+10s^3t+42s^2t^2+64st^3+32t^4)/8s^2$ and
  $(-t(s+t))(s^2+2t(s+t))/s^2$; their rate is Eq. (A12);
* Tang and Wu, their Table I at $m,M\to0$: $s^2/480$, $s^2/160$ and $s^2/40$ into a fermion pair from
  a scalar, a fermion and a massless vector, angle-integrated, with $\kappa^4=16/M_P^4$ taken out.

```{r published}
tt <- function(c) -(1 - c) / 2
G2pi2 <- 1 / 64
g314 <- function(c, mX = 0) { s <- 1; t <- tt(c); m2 <- mX^2
  8 * G2pi2 * (m2 - t) * (-m2 + s + t) * (-2 * m2 + s + 2 * t)^2 / s^2 }
g315 <- function(c, mX = 0) { s <- 1; t <- tt(c); m2 <- mX^2
  8 * G2pi2 / s^2 * (32 * m2^4 - 32 * m2^3 * (s + 4 * t) + 2 * m2^2 * (5 * s^2 + 64 * s * t + 96 * t^2) -
    4 * m2 * (s^3 + 13 * s^2 * t + 40 * s * t^2 + 32 * t^3) + s^4 + 10 * s^3 * t + 42 * s^2 * t^2 + 64 * s * t^3 + 32 * t^4) }
g316 <- function(c, mX = 0) { s <- 1; t <- tt(c); m2 <- mX^2; q <- m2^2 - 2 * m2 * t + t * (s + t)
  -32 * G2pi2 * q * (s^2 + 2 * q) / s^2 }
pub <- list(
  garny  = list(scalar = g314, dirac = g315, vector = g316),
  bernal = list(scalar = function(c) { t <- tt(c); (-t * (1 + t)) * (1 + 2 * t)^2 / 32 },
                dirac  = function(c) { t <- tt(c); (1 + 10 * t + 42 * t^2 + 64 * t^3 + 32 * t^4) / 128 },
                vector = function(c) { t <- tt(c); (-t * (1 + t)) * (1 + 2 * t * (1 + t)) / 8 }),
  clery  = list(scalar = function(c) { t <- tt(c); (-t * (1 + t)) * (1 + 2 * t)^2 / 4 },
                dirac  = function(c) { t <- tt(c); (1 + 10 * t + 42 * t^2 + 64 * t^3 + 32 * t^4) / 8 },
                vector = function(c) { t <- tt(c); (-t * (1 + t)) * (1 + 2 * t * (1 + t)) }))
## ratio of each printed squared amplitude to the helicity sum here, at five angles: the value farthest from the target
far <- function(v, target) v[which.max(abs(v - target))]
pr <- lapply(pub, function(p) sapply(names(p), function(ch) sapply(cs, function(c) p[[ch]](c) / spin_sum(ch, "dirac", c))))
gr <- t(pr$garny)       # kept for the planted errors
half <- c(scalar = 0.5, dirac = 1, vector = 0.5)              # the factor 1/2 for an identical pair
rowtxt <- list(
  self   = r"(| this paper | 1, 1, 1 | 1, 1, 1 | 22.5 Dirac | $1.20\times10^{-2}$ | 1 |)",
  garny  = r"(| 1/4, 1, 1/4 | 1/2, 2, 1/2 | 45 Dirac | none |)",
  bernal = r"(| 1/16 each | 1/16, 1/8, 1/16 | 45 Dirac | $1.06\times10^{-3}$ | 0.088 |)",
  clery  = r"(| 1, 1, 1 | 1, 2, 1 | 45 Dirac | $3.39\times10^{-2}$ | 1.41 |)",
  btv    = r"(| 1, 1, 29/12 | Table B.1 | 47 Weyl | $5.14\times10^{-2}$ | 2.14 |)")
chn <- c(scalar = "scalar", dirac = "fermion", vector = "gauge-boson")
## Garny et al.: squared amplitudes, then the channels in their rate (no 1/2 for an identical pair; 45 Dirac)
garny_sq <- c(scalar = 0.25, dirac = 1, vector = 0.25); garny_rate <- c(scalar = 0.5, dirac = 2, vector = 0.5)
for (ch in names(chn)) {
  r <- far(pr$garny[, ch], garny_sq[[ch]])
  chk(paste0("pub-g-", ch), "pub", sprintf("Garny et al. %s channel, squared amplitude over the one here", chn[[ch]]), r,
      garny_sq[[ch]], tol = 1e-12, label = as_fraction(garny_sq[[ch]]), quote = rowtxt$garny, where = "Table C.1")
  chk(paste0("pub-gr-", ch), "pub", sprintf("Garny et al. %s channel in their rate: squared amplitude x %s", chn[[ch]],
      if (ch == "dirac") "2 (45 Dirac)" else "2 (no 1/2 for the identical pair)"), r * 2, garny_rate[[ch]], tol = 1e-12,
      label = as_fraction(garny_rate[[ch]]), quote = rowtxt$garny, where = "Table C.1")
}
## Bernal et al.: squared amplitudes a sixteenth; their rate 1/16 of the 45-Dirac sum, so channels 1/16, 1/8, 1/16
for (ch in names(chn)) {
  r <- far(pr$bernal[, ch], 1 / 16)
  chk(paste0("pub-b-", ch), "pub", sprintf("Bernal et al. %s channel, squared amplitude over the one here", chn[[ch]]), r,
      1 / 16, tol = 1e-12, label = "1/16", quote = rowtxt$bernal, where = "Table C.1")
}
chk("pub-b-rate", "pub", "Bernal et al.'s Eq. (41) over alpha, per event", bernal_41 / alpha, "0.088", quote = rowtxt$bernal, where = "Table C.1")
## Clery et al.: squared amplitudes equal the ones here with the 1/2 for an identical pair
for (ch in names(chn)) {
  r <- far(pr$clery[, ch] / half[[ch]], 1)
  chk(paste0("pub-c-", ch), "pub", sprintf("Clery et al. %s channel over the one here%s", chn[[ch]],
      if (ch == "dirac") "" else " with 1/2 for the identical pair"), r, 1, tol = 1e-12, label = "1", quote = rowtxt$clery,
      where = "Table C.1")
}
chk("pub-c-coef", "pub", "Clery et al.'s Eq. (A12), 11351 pi^3/10368000", clery_A12, "3.39e-2", quote = rowtxt$clery, where = "Table C.1")
chk("pub-c-rate", "pub", "the same per event, over alpha", clery_A12 / 2 / alpha, "1.41", quote = rowtxt$clery, where = "Table C.1")
## Tang and Wu: angle-integrated channels in units of 16/M_P^4 (integral over cos(theta) only)
tw <- c(scalar = 1 / 480, dirac = 1 / 160, vector = 1 / 40)
for (ch in names(chn))
  chk(paste0("pub-t-", ch), "pub", sprintf("Tang and Wu %s channel: Int dcos sum|M|^2 / 16 here", chn[[ch]]), Kd[[ch]] / (2 * pi) / 16,
      tw[[ch]], rel = 1e-10, label = paste0("s^2/", 1 / tw[[ch]], " (quoted)"),
      quote = r"(scalar, a fermion and a gauge boson going to a fermion pair, $s^2/480$, $s^2/160$ and $s^2/40$, are ours)", where = "Appendix C")
## Boyle, Turok and Vaibhav: printed coefficient per event over alpha
chk("pub-btv-rate", "pub", "Boyle, Turok and Vaibhav as printed, per event, over alpha", btv() / 2 / alpha, "2.14", quote = rowtxt$btv, where = "Table C.1")
chk("pub-self", "pub", "this paper's coefficient", alpha, "1.20e-2", quote = rowtxt$self, where = "Table C.1")
## Verner: 45 times the amplitude averaged over the four initial spin states, against 22.5 Dirac sums
chk("pub-verner", "pub", "Verner's fermion weight, 45 x 1/4 of a Dirac sum, over 22.5", 45 / 4 / 22.5, 0.5, tol = 0, label = "1/2",
    quote = r"(which gives the fermion channel half its weight)", where = "Appendix C")
show_checks("pub")
garny_total <- sum(N_SM * per * garny_rate) / alpha
garny_total_half <- sum(N_SM * per * garny_rate * c(0.5, 1, 0.5)) / alpha
```

Garny et al. print no total. With the channel weights above their channels sum to
`r sprintf("%.3f", garny_total)` $\alpha$; read with the factor 1/2 for an identical pair, to
`r sprintf("%.3f", garny_total_half)` $\alpha$.

# Abundance from the plasma

Section 5: with $R=\alpha T^8/M_P^4$, $s=(2\pi^2/45)g_*T^3$ and $H=\sqrt{\pi^2g_*/90}\,T^2/M_P$, the
yield $dY/dT=-R/(sHT)$ integrates to $Y=(\alpha/C)(T_{\max}/M_P)^3$. The integral is done here by
quadrature as well as in closed form. Every number uses this report's $\alpha$ and $M_*$; the
author's `v6_bath.py` uses $\alpha=1.2\times10^{-2}$ and $M_*=4.916\times10^8$ GeV, rounded.

```{r abundance}
g <- K("gstar"); MP <- K("M_P")
CH <- sqrt(pi^2 * g / 90)
Cc <- 3 * (2 * pi^2 / 45) * g * CH
Tmax_test <- 3e15
Y_quad <- integrate(function(T) (alpha * T^8 / MP^4) / ((2 * pi^2 / 45) * g * T^3 * CH * T^2 / MP * T),
                    0, Tmax_test, rel.tol = 1e-12, abs.tol = 0)$value
Y_need <- rho_s / M_star
T_star <- MP * (Cc * Y_need / alpha)^(1 / 3)
T_HM <- sqrt(M_star * MP / CH)
over <- function(T) (alpha / Cc) * (T / MP)^3 / Y_need
n_eq <- 0.75 * (z3 / pi^2) * 2                     # Majorana N1 in equilibrium, two helicities, units T^3
Gamma_H <- alpha / (n_eq * CH)                      # R / (n_eq H) at T = M_P
M_at <- function(T) rho_s / ((alpha / Cc) * (T / MP)^3)
q_Tstar <- r"(a temperature 4.3 times the $1.87\times10^{13}$ GeV at which $H=M_*$, makes all the dark matter)"
chk("abund-1", "abund", "C = 3 (2 pi^2/45) g* sqrt(pi^2 g*/90)", Cc, "480.6", quote = r"(C=3\,\frac{2\pi^2}{45}\,g_*\sqrt{\frac{\pi^2g_*}{90}}=480.6)", where = "Section 5")
chk("abund-2", "abund", "Y by quadrature of dY/dT against (alpha/C)(T/M_P)^3", Y_quad / ((alpha / Cc) * (Tmax_test / MP)^3), 1,
    rel = 1e-10, label = "1", quote = r"(Y_{\rm grav}=\frac{\alpha}{C}\left(\frac{T_{\max}}{M_P}\right)^3)", where = "Section 5")
chk("abund-3", "abund", "yield needed at the ceiling, rho_DM/(s0 M_*)", Y_need, "8.9e-19", quote = r"(Y=\rho_{\rm DM,0}/(s_0M_*)=8.9\times10^{-19})", where = "Section 5")
chk("abund-4", "abund", "T_star, GeV", T_star, "8.0e13", quote = r"(T_\star=8.0\times10^{13}\ {\rm GeV})", where = "Section 5")
chk("abund-5", "abund", "T at which H = M_*, GeV", T_HM, "1.87e13", quote = q_Tstar, where = "Section 5")
chk("abund-6", "abund", "T_star over that", T_star / T_HM, "4.3", quote = q_Tstar, where = "Section 5")
chk("abund-7", "abund", "overproduction at 1e15 GeV", over(1e15), "1.95e3",
    quote = r"($1.95\times10^3$ times the observed dark matter at $10^{15}$ GeV)", where = "Section 5")
chk("abund-8", "abund", "overproduction at the reduced Planck temperature", over(MP), "2.8e13",
    quote = r"($2.8\times10^{13}$ times at $T=M_P$)", where = "Section 5")
chk("abund-9", "abund", "annihilation rate at the equilibrium density, R/n_eq, over H at T = M_P", Gamma_H, "1.9e-2",
    quote = r"($\Gamma=1.9\times10^{-2}H$)", where = "Section 5")
chk("abund-10", "abund", "mass if the plasma reached 1e16 GeV, GeV", M_at(1e16), "252",
    quote = r"(252 GeV if the plasma reached $10^{16}$ GeV)", where = "Section 5")
show_checks("abund")
```

The paper's rate of annihilation back to the plasma at the equilibrium density is, by detailed
balance, the production rate divided by that density, $\Gamma=R/n_{\rm eq}$ with
$n_{\rm eq}=\tfrac34\,(\zeta(3)/\pi^2)\,2\,T^3$ for a Majorana fermion, as in the author's
`v6_bath.py`. With the rounded inputs of `v6_bath.py`
($\alpha=1.2\times10^{-2}$, $M_*=4.916\times10^8$ GeV, $s_0=2.2215\times10^{-38}$ GeV$^3$),
$T_\star=$ `r tex_sci(MP * (Cc * (K("rho_DM") / K("s0_GeV3") / 4.916e8) / 1.2e-2)^(1/3), 4)` GeV and the
mass at $10^{16}$ GeV is `r sprintf("%.2f", K("rho_DM") / K("s0_GeV3") / ((1.2e-2 / Cc) * (1e16 / MP)^3))` GeV;
with this report's inputs they are `r tex_sci(T_star, 4)` GeV and `r sprintf("%.2f", M_at(1e16))` GeV.

# Higgs operator

Section 5's operator $(c_H/2\Lambda)\,\overline{N_1^c}N_1H^\dagger H$ shifts the Majorana mass term
$\tfrac12M\overline{N_1^c}N_1$ by $c_HH^\dagger H/\Lambda$. With $H^\dagger H=\tfrac12\sum_{a=1}^4\phi_a^2$
the vertex for $\phi_a\phi_a\to N_1N_1$ is $c_H/\Lambda$, the same normalisation that gives the
paper's $\Gamma(\phi\to N_1N_1)=y^2m_\phi/16\pi$ for $(y/2)\phi\overline{N_1^c}N_1$. The spin sum
$\sum|\bar u(k_3)v(k_4)|^2$ comes from the spinors above; the rate carries 1/2 for the identical
scalars, 1/2 for the identical Majorana pair and two $N_1$ per event, and with $|\mathcal M|^2\propto s$
the thermal integral takes the second moment $\int E^2f\,dE=2\zeta(3)$. The yield then follows
from $dY/dT=-R/(sHT)$ as for graviton exchange, now linear in $T_{\max}$.

```{r higgs}
## sum over the Majorana pair's spins of |ubar(k3) v(k4)|^2 at s = 1: should be 2 s, whatever the angle
uv2 <- function(c, phi = 0.3) { E <- 0.5; th <- acos(c); tot <- 0
  for (h3 in c(1, -1)) for (h4 in c(1, -1))
    tot <- tot + Mod(as.complex(dbar(u_sp(E, th, phi, h3)) %*% v_sp(E, pi - th, phi + pi, h4)))^2
  tot }
uv2_dev <- max(abs(sapply(c(-0.7, 0.1, 0.9), uv2) - 2))
J2 <- integrate(function(E) E^2 * fB(E), 0, Inf, rel.tol = 1e-12)$value
## number rate per real scalar, units c_H^2 T^6 / Lambda^2: 2 N1 per event x 1/2 x 1/2 x (1024 pi^6)^-1 x
## Int f1 f2 E1 E2 dE1 dE2 dcos12 [4 pi x 2 s], s = 2 E1 E2 (1 - cos12), Int (1 - cos12) dcos12 = 2
W2 <- hcubature(function(X) { E1 <- X[1, ]; E2 <- X[2, ]; s <- 2 * E1 * E2 * (1 - X[3, ])
  matrix(fB(E1) * fB(E2) * E1 * E2 * s, nrow = 1) }, c(0, 0, -1), c(50, 50, 1), tol = 1e-8, vectorInterface = TRUE)$integral
R_higgs <- 4 * 2 * 0.5 * 0.5 * 4 * pi * 2 * W2 / (1024 * pi^6)
R_higgs_cf <- 4 * 2 * 0.5 * 0.5 * 4 * pi * 2 * 2 * 2 * J2^2 / (1024 * pi^6)
r_higgs <- R_higgs / ((2 * pi^2 / 45) * g * CH)
c_all <- sqrt(Y_need / r_higgs)                         # T_max = Lambda = M_P
chk("higgs-1", "higgs", "sum |ubar v|^2 over the pair's spins, against 2s (largest error)", uv2_dev, 0, tol = 1e-14, label = "0", where = "identity")
chk("higgs-2", "higgs", "Int E^2/(e^E - 1) dE against 2 zeta(3)", J2, 2 * z3, rel = 1e-10, label = "2 zeta(3)", where = "closed form")
chk("higgs-3", "higgs", "rate by cubature against the closed form", R_higgs / R_higgs_cf, 1, rel = 1e-7, label = "1", where = "identity")
chk("higgs-4", "higgs", "yield coefficient, units c_H^2 T_max M_P / Lambda^2", r_higgs, "7.4e-6",
    quote = r"(yield, $7.4\times10^{-6}\,c_H^2\,T_{\max}M_P/\Lambda^2$, grows only as $T_{\max}$)", where = "Section 5")
chk("higgs-5", "higgs", "c_H that alone makes the dark matter at T_max = Lambda = M_P", c_all, "3.5e-7",
    quote = r"(if $c_H>3.5\times10^{-7}$ for $\Lambda=M_P$)", where = "Section 5")
chk("higgs-6", "higgs", "M_*/M_P", M_star / MP, "2e-10", quote = r"($c_H\sim M/\Lambda$, about $2\times10^{-10}$)", where = "Section 5")
show_checks("higgs")
```

# Einstein-Cartan contact term

Eliminating torsion with minimally coupled fermions leaves $-\tfrac3{16}A_\mu A^\mu/M_P^2$; the cross
term between a Standard Model Dirac current and that of $N_1$ is the amplitude
$\tfrac38\,[\bar v\gamma^\mu\gamma^5u][\bar u\gamma_\mu\gamma^5v]/M_P^2$, built from the same
spinors as the graviton amplitude.

```{r ec}
ec_shape <- function(c) (9 / 8) * (((1 - c) / 2)^2 + ((1 + c) / 2)^2)    # (9/8)(t^2 + u^2), s = 1
ec_cs <- c(-0.8, -0.1, 0.5, 0.95)
ec_dev <- max(abs(sapply(ec_cs, function(c) sum(Mod(contact_and_graviton(c)[, "contact"])^2)) - ec_shape(ec_cs)))
K_ec <- ang_int(function(c) sum(Mod(contact_and_graviton(c)[, "contact"])^2))
inter <- function(c) { m <- contact_and_graviton(c); sum(m[, "contact"] * Conj(m[, "graviton"])) }
inter_int <- max(abs(ang_int(function(c) Re(inter(c)))), abs(ang_int(function(c) Im(inter(c)))))
inter_fixed <- Mod(inter(0.5))
alpha_EC <- 22.5 * per[["dirac"]] * K_ec / Kd[["dirac"]]
T_star_EC <- MP * (Cc * Y_need / (alpha + alpha_EC))^(1 / 3)
## Shaposhnikov et al., PRL 126 (2021) 161301, Eq. (9): Omega_N/Omega_DM = 3.6e-2 C_M (M/10 keV)(T/M_P)^3,
## C_M = (9/4)(24 a^4 + 21 b+^4) = (9/4) 45 for a Majorana N with alpha = beta = 0 (their Eq. 6)
alpha_SST <- 3.6e-2 * (9 / 4) * 45 / 1e-5 * rho_s * Cc
q_ec <- r"($\sum|\mathcal M|^2=\tfrac98(t^2+u^2)/M_P^4$ per Dirac pair, which integrates over angle to $3\pi$, fifteen times the graviton's Dirac channel)"
q_ec2 <- r"(it gives $7.42\times10^{-2}$, 6.17 times $\alpha$)"
chk("ec-1", "ec", "largest |sum|M|^2 - (9/8)(t^2+u^2)| at four angles", ec_dev, 0, tol = 1e-14, label = "0", quote = q_ec, where = "Appendix B")
chk("ec-2", "ec", "angular integral", K_ec, 3 * pi, rel = 1e-10, label = "3 pi", quote = q_ec, where = "Appendix B")
chk("ec-3", "ec", "over the graviton's Dirac channel", K_ec / Kd[["dirac"]], 15, rel = 1e-10, label = "15", quote = q_ec, where = "Appendix B")
chk("ec-4", "ec", "alpha_EC with 22.5 Dirac fermions", alpha_EC, "7.42e-2", quote = q_ec2, where = "Appendix B")
chk("ec-5", "ec", "alpha_EC over alpha", alpha_EC / alpha, "6.17", quote = q_ec2, where = "Appendix B")
chk("ec-6", "ec", "alpha_EC over alpha (Section 5)", alpha_EC / alpha, "6.2",
    quote = r"(it adds $7.42\times10^{-2}\,T^8/M_P^4$, 6.2 times $\alpha$)", where = "Section 5")
chk("ec-7", "ec", "T_star with the contact term added, GeV", T_star_EC, "4.2e13",
    quote = r"(and lowers $T_\star$ to $4.2\times10^{13}$ GeV)", where = "Section 5")
chk("ec-8", "ec", "interference with graviton exchange, integrated over angle", inter_int, 0, tol = 1e-12, label = "0",
    quote = r"(so their interference integrates to zero over angle)", where = "Appendix B")
chk("ec-9", "ec", "the same at c = 0.5 is not zero (1 = yes)", as.numeric(inter_fixed > 1e-6), 1, tol = 0, label = "1",
    quote = r"(and that it is not zero at fixed angle)", where = "Appendix B")
chk("ec-10", "ec", "Shaposhnikov et al.'s formula over alpha_EC, excess in per cent (claim: about 3)", 100 * (alpha_SST / alpha_EC - 1), 3,
    tol = 0.5, label = "about 3", quote = r"(3 per cent below what Shaposhnikov et al.'s abundance formula gives without non-minimal couplings)", where = "Appendix B")
show_checks("ec")
```

$T_\star$ with the contact term is `r tex_sci(T_star_EC, 5)` GeV, which rounds to the printed
$4.2\times10^{13}$ with `r tex_sci(T_star_EC - 4.15e13, 2)` GeV to spare. Shaposhnikov et al.'s formula gives
`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * (alpha_SST / alpha_EC - 1))` per cent more than the contact rate here,
against the paper's "3 per cent"; their coefficient $3.6\times10^{-2}$ is printed to two
digits, which alone carries about 1.4 per cent into the comparison.

# Statistics and the KMS relation

Appendix B describes the rate through the plasma's stress-tensor Wightman function, whose two-body
part carries $f_1f_2$; the weight for the plasma to take energy carries $(1\pm f_1)(1\pm f_2)$, which
by the KMS relation equals $e^{(E_1+E_2)/T}f_1f_2$. As a cross-check of Table B.1, the same rate in
Maxwell-Boltzmann statistics, where each moment $\int E^3f\,dE$ becomes $\Gamma(4)=6$, is 0.961 of
$\alpha$, the $1.1560\times10^{-2}$ of that table.

```{r classical}
kms <- 0
for (a in c(0.3, 1, 4)) for (b in c(0.5, 2, 7))
  kms <- max(kms, abs((1 + fB(a)) * (1 + fB(b)) / (exp(a + b) * fB(a) * fB(b)) - 1),
             abs((1 - fF(a)) * (1 - fF(b)) / (exp(a + b) * fF(a) * fF(b)) - 1))
ratio_mb <- ours_mb / alpha
ratio_mb_cf <- sum(N_SM * w_ch * Kd * 36) / sum(N_SM * w_ch * Kd * c(JB, JF, JB)^2)
chk("cl-1", "cl", "KMS: (1 +- f1)(1 +- f2) / (e^(E1+E2) f1 f2) - 1, largest", kms, 0, tol = 1e-12, label = "0", where = "identity")
chk("cl-2", "cl", "classical gas (Maxwell-Boltzmann, cubature) over alpha", ratio_mb, "0.961", where = "cross-check")
chk("cl-3", "cl", "the same from the moments, 36 over J1 J2", ratio_mb_cf, "0.961", where = "cross-check")
show_checks("cl")
```

# Planted errors

Each planted error below pushes one wrong input through the same calculation as a check above and
compares the result with that check's paper value and tolerance. Every one must fail. The summary
table at the end also moves every computed value by at least 1 per cent and 2.5 tolerances and shows
that the comparison then fails.

```{r plants}
## alpha with the 45 Weyl fermions counted as 45 Dirac fermions
plant("p-1", "therm-12", "alpha with 45 Dirac fermions in place of 22.5", S45)
plant("p-2", "therm-11", "alpha off by 1 per cent", 1.01 * alpha)
## real-scalar stress tensor with Garny et al.'s factor 1/2
plant("p-3", "hel-4", "real-scalar stress tensor halved", ang_int(function(c) {
  Ti <- 0.5 * initial_T("scalar")[[1]]; sum(sapply(final_T("dirac", c), function(Tf) Mod(amp(Ti, Tf))^2)) }))
## fermion stress tensor built with k = p1 + p2 in place of p1 - p2
plant("p-4", "hel-5", "fermion stress tensor with k = p1 + p2", ang_int(function(c) {
  E <- 0.5; tot <- 0
  for (h1 in c(1, -1)) for (h2 in c(1, -1)) {
    vb <- dbar(v_sp(E, pi, 0, h2)); u <- u_sp(E, 0, 0, h1); k <- mom(E, 0, 0) + mom(E, pi, 0)
    J <- vapply(GAM, function(g) as.complex(vb %*% g %*% u), 0i); Ti <- 0.25 * (outer(J, k) + outer(k, J))
    for (Tf in final_T("dirac", c)) tot <- tot + Mod(amp(Ti, Tf))^2 }
  tot }))
## gauge vertex cut down to its (p1.p2)(e1 e2 + e2 e1) term, which is not built from field strengths
part_vertex <- function(p1, e1, p2, e2) mdot(p1, p2) * (outer(e1, e2) + outer(e2, e1))
plant("p-5", "hel-10", "gauge vertex with only its (p1.p2)(e1 e2 + e2 e1) term, e -> p", max(sapply(final_T("dirac", 0.4),
  function(Tf) Mod(amp(part_vertex(p1, p1, p2, eps_h(pi, 0, 1)), Tf)))))
## Bose-Einstein moment for the fermions
plant("p-6", "therm-8", "fermions given the Bose-Einstein moment", Kd[["dirac"]] * (32 / 3) * JB^2 / (1024 * pi^6))
## no 1/2 for identical initial bosons
plant("p-7", "therm-7", "no 1/2 for identical initial scalars", Kd[["scalar"]] * (32 / 3) * JB^2 / (1024 * pi^6))
## conformal coupling mistyped as 0.2
plant("p-8", "tab1-scalar16-1", "scalar dark matter with xi = 0.2 in place of 1/6",
      0.5 * 0.5 * ang_int(function(c) spin_sum("scalar", "scalar", c, xi_out = 0.2)) * (32 / 3) * JB^2 / (1024 * pi^6) / pi^3)
plant("p-9", "pub-g-dirac", "Garny et al.'s Eq. (3.15) read with an extra factor 2", far(2 * gr["dirac", ], 1))
## the in-vacuum's production integral in place of the half-angle state's
plant("p-10", "mass-2", "M_* from I_in in place of I_*", mass_from_I(I_in_cf) / 1e6)
## occupation without the factor 1/2
plant("p-11", "mode-6", "I_* with n = 1 - sqrt(1 - P), no 1/2", 2 * I_star_cf)
## the after-vacuum: how far it sits below n_*
plant("p-12", "lem-6", "the after-vacuum, which is not invariant", (1 - sqrt(1 - 0.5)) / 2)
## upper edge of the family taken as n_* (no excursion)
plant("p-13", "floor-4b", "upper edge replaced by the half-angle state", I_state(0) / I_star_cf)
## C with g* = 110.25
plant("p-14", "abund-1", "C with g* = 110.25", 3 * (2 * pi^2 / 45) * 110.25 * sqrt(pi^2 * 110.25 / 90))
## T_star with the 45-Dirac rate
plant("p-15", "abund-4", "T_star with the 45-Dirac rate", MP * (Cc * Y_need / S45)^(1 / 3))
## contact coupling 3/16 in place of 3/8
plant("p-16", "ec-2", "contact amplitude with 3/16 in place of 3/8",
      ang_int(function(c) sum(Mod(contact_and_graviton(c, coupling = 3 / 16)[, "contact"])^2)))
## Maxwell-Boltzmann moment Gamma(3) = 2 in place of Gamma(4) = 6
plant("p-17", "cl-3", "classical-gas moment 2 in place of 6", sum(N_SM * w_ch * Kd * 4) / sum(N_SM * w_ch * Kd * c(JB, JF, JB)^2))
## their printed spin-1 coefficient replaced by the transverse one before the first step
plant("p-18", "btv-5", "Boyle, Turok and Vaibhav with A = 12 already in the first row", btv(A = c(4, 3, 12)) / alpha)
## Clery's Eq. (A12) compared with alpha in place of the 45-Dirac sum
plant("p-19", "dbl-4", "Eq. (A12) over alpha in place of the 45-Dirac sum", clery_A12 / alpha)
## a missing value must fail
plant("p-20", "mass-2", "a missing value", NA_real_)

pl <- REG$plants
html_table(data.frame(
  ID = names(pl), `Against check` = vapply(pl, `[[`, "", "check_id"),
  `Planted error` = vapply(pl, function(p) html_escape(p$what), ""),
  `Planted value` = vapply(pl, function(p) fmt(p$planted), ""),
  `Paper` = vapply(pl, function(p) REG$checks[[p$check_id]]$shown, ""),
  Verdict = vapply(pl, `[[`, "", "verdict"),
  Caught = vapply(pl, function(p) if (p$caught) "yes" else "<b>NO</b>", ""),
  check.names = FALSE))
```

$T_\star$ goes as $\alpha^{-1/3}$, so an error of 1 per cent in $\alpha$ moves it by 0.3 per cent,
inside its printed precision; the check of $\alpha$ itself catches that error (p-2), and the
45-Dirac count moves $T_\star$ far enough to fail (p-15).

# Author's checker

The author's `v6_numbers_check.py` pairs each sentence of the paper with the output of the script
that makes its number. It runs here last, if python3 with numpy and scipy is present and the
author's scripts are found at `../../far_side/calc` (working tree) or `../../checks/calc` (public
release). The project's virtual environment, `../../.venv/bin/python3`, is preferred when it
exists.

```{r author-checker}
py <- file.path("..", "..", ".venv", "bin", "python3")
if (!file.exists(py)) py <- unname(Sys.which("python3"))
calc_dirs <- c(file.path("..", "..", "far_side", "calc"), file.path("..", "..", "checks", "calc"))
calc_found <- calc_dirs[file.exists(file.path(calc_dirs, "v6_grav_rate.py"))]
why_skip <- NULL
if (!nzchar(py)) {
  why_skip <- "python3 was not found."
} else if (!file.exists("v6_numbers_check.py")) {
  why_skip <- "v6_numbers_check.py is not in this directory."
} else if (!length(calc_found)) {
  why_skip <- "the author's scripts are in neither ../../far_side/calc nor ../../checks/calc."
} else {
  mods <- suppressWarnings(system2(py, c("-c", shQuote("import numpy, scipy")), stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE,
                                   env = "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1"))
  if (!is.null(attr(mods, "status")) && attr(mods, "status") != 0)
    why_skip <- paste("python3 at", py, "lacks numpy or scipy.")
}
author_status <- NA
if (is.null(why_skip)) {
  t_py <- Sys.time()
  out <- suppressWarnings(system2(py, "v6_numbers_check.py", stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE,
                                  env = "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1", timeout = params$author_checker_timeout))
  author_status <- if (is.null(attr(out, "status"))) 0L else attr(out, "status")
  cat(sprintf("python: %s\nscripts: %s\nexit status: %d (%s)\ntime: %.1f s\nlast lines:\n\n", py, calc_found[1], author_status,
              if (author_status == 0) "no problems" else if (author_status == 124) "timed out" else "problems reported",
              as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t_py, units = "secs"))))
  cat(tail(out, 15), sep = "\n")
} else {
  cat("Skipped:", why_skip, "\n")
}
```

# Summary

```{r summary-counts, echo = FALSE}
ck <- REG$checks
n_pass <- sum(vapply(ck, `[[`, TRUE, "ok"))
gp <- lapply(ck, generic_plant)
n_gcaught <- sum(vapply(gp, `[[`, TRUE, "caught"))
n_pcaught <- sum(vapply(REG$plants, `[[`, TRUE, "caught"))
fails <- names(ck)[!vapply(ck, `[[`, TRUE, "ok")]
q_state <- vapply(ck, function(r) in_paper(r$quote), "")
n_quoted <- sum(nzchar(q_state)); n_found <- sum(q_state == "yes")
run_time <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), T_START, units = "secs"))
cpu <- proc.time() - CPU_START
cpu_r <- cpu[["user.self"]] + cpu[["sys.self"]]
cpu_child <- sum(cpu[c("user.child", "sys.child")], na.rm = TRUE)
```

**`r length(ck)` checks: `r n_pass` PASS, `r length(ck) - n_pass` FAIL**`r if (length(fails)) paste0(" (", paste(fails, collapse = ", "), ")") else ""`.
Planted errors caught: `r n_gcaught` of `r length(ck)` generic plants, one per check, and
`r n_pcaught` of `r length(REG$plants)` named plants. `r if (is.na(PAPER_TEXT)) "Quoted words not checked: no paper source found beside this file." else sprintf("Quoted words found in the paper source: %d of %d.", n_found, n_quoted)` Author's checker:
`r if (is.null(why_skip)) sprintf("exit status %d.", author_status) else paste("skipped,", why_skip)`
Processor time `r sprintf("%.0f", cpu_r)` s in R and `r sprintf("%.0f", cpu_child)` s in the author's
checker; `r sprintf("%.0f", run_time)` s on the clock.

```{r summary-table, echo = FALSE}
named <- split(names(REG$plants), vapply(REG$plants, `[[`, "", "check_id"))
html_table(size = "85%", data.frame(
  ID = names(ck),
  Check = vapply(ck, function(r) html_escape(r$what), ""),
  Computed = vapply(ck, function(r) fmt(r$computed), ""),
  Paper = vapply(ck, `[[`, "", "shown"),
  Tolerance = vapply(ck, function(r) fmt(r$tol, 2), ""),
  Verdict = vapply(ck, function(r) if (r$ok) "PASS" else "<b>FAIL</b>", ""),
  `Generic plant` = vapply(names(ck), function(i) paste0(fmt(gp[[i]]$planted), ": ",
                           if (gp[[i]]$caught) "FAIL, caught" else "<b>PASS, not caught</b>"), ""),
  `Named plants` = vapply(names(ck), function(i) {
    ids <- named[[i]]
    if (is.null(ids)) "" else paste(vapply(ids, function(p) paste0(p, if (REG$plants[[p]]$caught) " caught" else " <b>NOT caught</b>"), ""), collapse = "; ")
  }, ""),
  check.names = FALSE))
```
